Title: Chow: Penang must maximise existing land to drive state revenue
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang must maximise its limited land resources by focusing on development with the greatest economic impact, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
Responding to claims by Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli that Penang's limited land was contributing to lower state revenue compared with larger states such as Johor, Chow said the issue was already being addressed through the Penang Structure Plan 2040.
"Refer to this. The solution is here," Chow said when asked how Penang could overcome its land constraints.
Chow said the state was continuously acquiring land and opening up areas for industrial and other uses, while rezoning rural areas as urban areas was another way to optimise land use.
"There are plans for land development here. We are always in the process of acquiring and opening up land for industries and various uses, not just industries," he added.
Chow said Penang could not escape its geographical constraints and therefore needed to plan development based on the state's strengths and limitations.
"We have to work within the constraints of the state. We have our advantages and disadvantages, so we need to plan according to our strengths and weaknesses," he said.
He added that Seberang Prai, which still had more available land, could play a role in future development under the 2040 plan.
Yesterday, during a gathering with Bersama leaders and members in Penang, Rafizi said
Penang's dwindling land resources could create a long-term revenue challenge for the state government.
He said the issue was not about the performance of any particular chief minister, but a structural problem arising from the state's limited land and the way revenue is divided between state and federal governments.
Rafizi said the state's revenue was heavily linked to land, including land premiums, while other major sources of taxation were under the jurisdiction of the Federal Government.
He said this posed a particular challenge for a relatively small state such as Penang compared with larger states with more extensive land resources.
"Once the land is gone, the state government's biggest source of revenue, which is land premiums, is gone," he said.

Title: Myanmar confirms nearly 309,000 Rohingya in Bangladesh, security issues delaying repatriation
Article:
YANGON: Myanmar's military-backed government has verified that nearly 309,000 displaced people in camps in Bangladesh are former residents of the troubled Rakhine State, but repatriation will proceed only after security in Rakhine improves, the foreign ministry said.
Myanmar has verified 308,797 displaced people in Bangladesh as former Rakhine residents out of 828,824 names submitted as of July 31, 2026, the foreign ministry said in a statement over the weekend.
According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 Rohingya fled to neighbouring Bangladesh in 2017 after a crackdown by Myanmar security forces, and many more are still leaving via uncertain sea and land journeys.
Myanmar says it has identified 4,241 people on Bangladesh's repatriation list it alleged were involved in terrorist activities, while a further 113,507 could not be verified.
Myanmar says repatriation will begin only when security conditions in Rakhine State become more stable.
Myanmar's military is fighting the Arakan Army, an ethnic armed group based in Rakhine that has sought greater autonomy for the region.
Myanmar says repatriation is strictly a bilateral matter with Bangladesh.
Myanmar says previous repatriation arrangements in 2018 and 2019 resulted in no returnees despite bilateral preparations.
Myanmar agreed to take back 5,000 Rohingya asylum seekers from Malaysia, but Malaysia said the repatriation would not proceed if lives were at risk.

Title: Chow: Penang Third Link remains in 2040 state structure plan
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang's proposed third link remains on the cards, with the project included indicatively in the Penang Structure Plan 2040.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the proposed third bridge or undersea tunnel remained in the plan as the agreement for the project was still valid.
"It is still there. The agreement is still valid. We have already given the offer to the company," he said after launching the public participation and public notification programme for the Penang Structure Plan 2040 here today.
State Infrastructure, Transport and Utility Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari, in his winding-up speech
during the state legislative assembly sitting
last year, said the state government was considering changing the proposed design from an undersea tunnel to a bridge across the Penang Straits.
Penang already has two bridges, with the second bridge currently underutilised.
Chow, however, said the inclusion was indicative and did not mean construction would immediately take place.
He said the timing of development would depend on the government and private sector, depending on their respective development plans.
"Many development areas or development zones are placed indicatively. When they are developed, sometimes it depends on the government and sometimes on the private sector," he added.
Chow said the structure plan was a high-level planning document outlining the state's future direction, while more specific development proposals would be covered under local plans.
He said the plan was important to ensure balanced development between Penang island and Seberang Prai, while taking into account environmental sustainability and disaster risks.
On Pulau Jerejak, Chow said more than 80 acres of privately owned land were involved in development plans, while the remaining areas remained gazetted as permanent forest reserves.
He said infrastructure and utility projects could still be considered within permanent forest reserves, but other forms of development would not be allowed.

Title: Chow: Penang's draft 2040 plan not perfect, public views welcome
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang's draft 2040 state structure plan is not perfect, and public views will be taken seriously before it is finalised, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the draft Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (Review) is open to scrutiny, with constructive views and proposals from the public and stakeholders needed to improve the document.
"Draft RSN 2040 is not a document that we consider perfect. Instead, we are opening space for the people to scrutinise it, give their views, put forward proposals and, if necessary, challenge any proposal based on facts, expertise and the public interest," he said at the launch of the publicity and public participation programme here today.
Chow said all views received would be carefully considered and serve as important input before the document was finalised for approval and gazettement.
He said the public participation phase, launched today, is crucial in determining the state's development direction over the next 15 years.
"Development planning is not merely the responsibility of the government. It is a shared responsibility," he said.
He said public and stakeholder input was important to ensure development was based not only on data and studies but also reflected the needs and aspirations of the people.
The draft plan is intended to replace the Penang State Structure Plan 2030, which was gazetted on Oct 24, 2019, in line with the Town and Country Planning Act 1976 (Act 172).
Chow said Penang had since experienced rapid growth as a major economic, industrial and technology hub, but this had also brought increasingly complex challenges, including climate change, floods, pressure on land and water resources, affordable housing, the cost of living, mobility, and changes in technology and the digital economy.
He said the draft RSN 2040 aimed to ensure Penang's growth was more organised, competitive, sustainable and liveable, while continuing to be guided by the Penang2030 vision, federal policies and Malaysia Madani aspirations.
Among its key areas of focus are balanced development between the island and Seberang Prai, optimal land use, strengthening growth centres, transit-oriented development, transport networks, housing, economic competitiveness and environmental protection.
On mobility, Chow said public transport development must keep pace with the state's growth.
He cited the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project as one of the strategic plans to improve connectivity, encourage transit-oriented development and support low-carbon mobility.
He also said large-scale developments, including Silicon Island, must be assessed comprehensively to ensure economic growth, infrastructure, jobs, housing, mobility and environmental sustainability progressed in balance.
Chow urged Penangites, ministries and departments, local authorities, the private sector, academia, professional bodies, non-governmental organisations and other stakeholders to study the draft and submit constructive views and recommendations.
"What we plan today will determine the face of Penang in 2040 and for generations after that. Penang 2040 is not merely the vision of the state government; it is our shared future," he said.

Title: Safeguarding Malaysia's Blue Economy
Article:
A TOTAL of RM823.88 million is the estimated value of Malaysia's fisheries resources lost to the intrusion of foreign fishing vessels between 2020 and 2023.
Addressing illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is not just an enforcement matter but an essential step in protecting Malaysia's natural capital.
Malaysia's seas are worth far more than the sum of their catch; they are fundamental to our food security, local livelihoods, and the country's burgeoning Blue Economy.
The Department of Fisheries Malaysia has noted that the losses are based on recorded enforcement cases, supported by proxy data and international guidelines.
The figures offer an important baseline, but the full ecological and economic cost is difficult to quantify. This is where maritime intelligence can introduce a vital new dimension to Malaysia's security efforts.
It involves understanding the broader picture, which includes identifying who is operating, where vessels are heading, and recognising behavioural shifts that signal potential risks. This requires connecting diverse streams of information, including vessel tracking, satellite imagery, fishing licences, and historical records, to transform raw data into actionable intelligence.
For instance, a vessel that repeatedly disables its tracking system or loiters near protected grounds exhibits patterns that may serve as an early warning for monitoring authorities. This approach requires the inclusion of our most important asset, which is our coastal fishermen and residents as watchful guardians of our waters.
Fostering a collaborative framework where local maritime knowledge is integrated with satellite-driven intelligence can create a robust ecosystem of "smarter eyes" at sea.
When the firsthand observations of our coastal communities meet the sophisticated insights of data analytics, the resulting intelligence is more precise and proactive. Preventing an incursion before it crosses into national waters protects fish stocks, marine habitats, and the livelihoods of local fishermen who rely on these grounds.
While the number of detentions and the value of seized catches are important metrics, success should also be measured by indicators such as earlier detection, fewer repeat incursions, and the long-term health of our fish stocks.
The prosperity of our Blue Economy may well depend not only on how we respond to intruders, but on how intelligently and collaboratively we anticipate them.
DR MOHD ROZAIMY RIDZUAN
Lecturer,
Faculty of Administrative Science and Policy Studies,
UiTM Pahang Branch, Raub Campus
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kenanga maintains ringgit forecast of RM3.95 to US dollar by year-end
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd (Kenanga IB) has retained its ringgit forecast of RM3.95 to the US dollar by year-end, underpinned by resilient growth, a sustained current account (CA) surplus and record foreign-currency deposits.
In a research note today, the investment bank said it holds its constructive medium-term stance as the US dollar's elevated level looks increasingly like a temporary risk-premium bump rather than a new trend.
Kenanga IB attributed the greenback's strength to Middle East jitters and markets pushing out United States Federal Reserve (Fed) cuts while still pricing some chance of further hikes.
"The structural case for a weaker US dollar over time, supported by reserve diversification, still-wide US fiscal deficits and gradual portfolio reallocation, should reassert once the Fed moves from pause to actual easing," it said.
In the near term, Kenanga IB said, the pause should keep the US dollar underpinned on rate differentials; the pivot to easing should then renew downward pressure.
It also said that the ringgit's nominal effective exchange rate fell 0.8 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026) even as the US dollar/ringgit pair held broadly steady, highlighting some trade-weighted weakness.
"Still, resilient growth, a sustained CA surplus and record foreign-currency deposits remain supportive, and we retain RM3.95 as the likelier outcome," it said.
Meanwhile, Kenanga IB said Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to hold the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent through 2026.
"Inflation is contained enough to keep pre-emptive tightening off the table, though pipeline pressures warrant closer monitoring," it said.
It noted that headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent in Q2 2026 from 1.6 per cent in the first quarter (Q1), largely on a jump in fuel inflation to 5.0 per cent as RON97 and diesel prices moved higher, while core inflation eased to 1.9 per cent from 2.1 per cent in Q1 2026.
Additionally, it said while Q2 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 6.0 per cent remained above Bank Negara's 4.0-5.0 per cent 2026 guidance range, the central bank is expected to look through the current cost shock and preserve policy flexibility unless stronger growth or inflation pressures trigger persistent second-round effects.
Meanwhile, Apex Securities Bhd also expects the central bank to keep the OPR on hold at 2.75 per cent through 2026, saying Bank Negara is likely to adopt a wait-and-see approach and assess the rising headwinds in the second half of 2026.
"Our 2026 baseline GDP growth forecast of 5.0 per cent and inflation forecast of 2.0 per cent also remain within Bank Negara's current projections," it said.
However, it noted that with full-year GDP growth potentially reaching 5.1-5.5 per cent year-on-year, above Bank Negara's current forecast range, the stronger-than-expected performance in the first half of 2026 has raised the prospect of a rate hike.

Title: RM900,000 Bentley payout legal battle was about integrity, says businessmam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A businessman whose RM900,000 insurance payout for his Bentley was upheld by the Court of Appeal says his legal battle with MSIG Insurance (M) Bhd was ultimately about clearing his name.
Inderpal Singh said he was deeply insulted by the insurer's suggestion that he had deliberately staged the accident to make an insurance claim.
"What made it even harder to comprehend was that the accident took place within Tropicana Golf & Country Resort, one of Petaling Jaya's most heavily guarded neighbourhoods, with three security checkpoints.
"Apparently, I was supposed to have engineered the entire accident there.
"Quite an extraordinary choice of location for anyone supposedly planning to stage an accident," he said in a Facebook post.
He also questioned the suggestion that he had staged the accident because he could not afford a Bentley, pointing out that he owned a Rolls-Royce.
"The logic behind that suggestion was, frankly, absurd," he said.
Inderpal said he was summoned by MSIG's head of claims and described the questioning as unnecessarily arrogant and dismissive.
He said he was being treated as though he had something to hide.
"The investigation left me feeling that the objective was not to establish the truth, but to create doubt about my character and to portray me as dishonest and deceitful.
"We pay our insurance premiums in good faith, trusting that when a claim arises, it will be assessed fairly, professionally and without bias.
"Instead, I was subjected to a process that felt less like an objective assessment of facts and more like a predetermined interrogation. One that appeared designed to cast suspicion first, and seek justification later," he said.
Inderpal said allegations questioning a person's honesty and integrity could cause damage beyond the financial value of an insurance claim.
He said the
appellate court's decision to uphold the RM900,000
award was significant as the court did not accept the suggestion that the accident had been staged.
"But for me, this was never really about RM900,000.
"It was about having my name questioned. My integrity questioned. My truth questioned," he said.
He added that some battles were fought for money while others were fought for one's reputation.
"The latter is the battle you never forget.
"Because in the end, an insurance claim can be measured in ringgit. But a person's name cannot," he said.
He said he had chosen to let the judgment speak for itself, describing the court decision as the strongest vindication.
On Friday, a three-member Court of Appeal bench led by Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, with Datuk Ismail Brahim and Datuk Leonard David Shim, upheld the High Court's decision ordering MSIG to pay Inderpal RM900,000 for damage to his Bentley six years ago.
Choo said they found nothing plainly wrong which warranted an interference and not convinced by MSIG's suggestion that the accident had been staged to make an insurance claim.
He said accidents could occasionally happen without a scientific or logical explanation.
MSIG had contended that Inderpal failed to prove that the incident was an accidental collision.
Lawyers David Samuel and Mithurran Ravinthiran represented Inderpal, while Samreet Singh Sagoo and Theebadarshini Retnakumar acted for MSIG.
The matter arose after MSIG rejected Inderpal's claim for damage to his Bentley, which was comprehensively insured for RM900,000 from Feb 8, 2019 to Feb 7, 2020.
The Bentley was damaged in a single-vehicle accident at Jalan Tropicana Utama, Petaling Jaya, on Jan 22, 2020.
At 11.31pm, Inderpal was driving from his sister's residence in Kelana Jaya to his home when, while negotiating a right-hand bend in light rain or drizzle, he encountered a puddle and a dog crossing his path.
The Bentley lost control, struck a guardrail on the left side of the road, passed beneath or through the weakened structure and came to rest behind it.
The following day, he notified MSIG's insurance agent, lodged a police report and sent the Bentley to an authorised workshop, which assessed the repair cost at RM1,053,491.07.
MSIG rejected the claim on June 4, 2021, alleging that the accident was suspicious and involved fraudulent means, cheating, criminal breach of trust and false information.
However, the High Court, in its judgment dated May 20 last year, found that the accident occurred as reported and that MSIG had failed to prove the claim was fraudulent.

Title: Maybank to support Haier in Asean's smart energy solutions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) is collaborating with China's Haier Group to support the expansion of the latter's new energy platform and ecosystem across Southeast Asia.
In a statement today, Maybank said that it has entered into a Heads of Agreement (HoA) with Haier Energy Sdn Bhd, to form a strategic partnership aimed at accelerating the adoption of smart energy solutions across the region.
Under the HoA, Maybank will leverage its regional business banking platform, Maybank2E and its comprehensive suite of products and services to support Haier Energy's expansion and facilitate supply chain agility.
Specifically, the collaboration will encompass integrated transaction banking, payments and financing solutions, including credit card partnerships and financing facilities for retail clients, Islamic financing, sustainability finance, supply chain financing, cash management, trade finance, treasury and foreign exchange services.
The partnership presents an exciting opportunity to Maybank, due to demand for investments to strengthen regional energy resilience, as well as continued expansions of companies seeking to diversify away from China and expand into Asean.
"The partnership with Haier Energy aligns with Maybank's commitment to playing a bigger role in ASEAN's energy transition and the China-ASEAN economic corridor, where China is one of ASEAN's top investors and trading partners," said Datuk John Chong, Maybank's group CEO of global banking in the statement.
Haier Energy general manager Ji Xiaojian said Asean represents a key growth market for the company, given its strong economic expansion and rising demand for smart energy generation, storage and infrastructure solutions.
Haier Group currently serves more than one billion households worldwide and operates 133 manufacturing facilities and 71 research and development centres globally, underscoring its scale and capabilities in advancing sustainable energy technologies.

Title: Affin Bank misses estimates as provisions rise, says CIMB Securities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Bank Bhd's first-half 2026 core net profit fell 1.7 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM263.0 million, coming in below CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd's expectations as higher provisions weighed on its second-quarter performance.
The bank's second-quarter net profit declined 11.1 per cent YoY, with net credit charge (NCC) rising to 38 basis points, significantly above the 13 basis points assumed for the full year.
The first-half results accounted for only 45 per cent of the firm's full-year earnings forecast and 46 per cent of consensus estimates.
Despite provisions rising 142.2 per cent YoY, Affin's operating income grew 12.2 per cent, supported by a 17.4 per cent increase in fund-based income and a 3.4 per cent rise in non-interest income.
Loan growth remained strong at 13.6 per cent, led by corporate banking, enterprise banking and community banking.
NIM also improved three basis points YoY to 1.52 per cent, while the cost-to-income ratio fell to 63 per cent from 68.9 per cent.
However, second-quarter net profit fell 5.9 per cent quarter-on-quarter as non-interest income declined 12.5 per cent and provisions rose another 14.4 per cent.
Affin said NIM could have been higher without the delayed drawdown of a sizeable high-yielding loan.
The bank's gross impaired loan ratio rose to 1.82 per cent in the second quarter from 1.75 per cent, although CIMB Securities said this did not indicate broad-based asset quality deterioration, with stress concentrated in the retail segment, particularly mortgages, hire purchase and credit cards.
The firm raised its NCC assumptions for 2026, 2027 and 2028 to 38.5, 27.0 and 21.2 basis points, respectively, from 12.9, 14.6 and 20 basis points previously.
It said Affin now expects NCC to remain materially above its earlier guidance of around 13 basis points, amid emerging stress from Covid-19 legacy mortgages, the hire-purchase portfolio and credit card delinquencies linked to rising individual cost-of-living pressures.
Consequently, earnings forecasts for 2026, 2027 and 2028 were cut by seven per cent, 5.6 per cent and 11.5 per cent, respectively.
CIMB Securities also streamlined its NIM forecasts to 1.53 per cent for 2026 to 2028 while raising its non-interest income projections by 14 per cent to 22 per cent on stronger fee income and investment income.
The firm downgraded Affin to "Hold" from the "Buy" call and lowered its target price to RM2.30 from RM2.82, based on a lower 2026 forecast price-to-book value multiple of 0.48 times from 0.59 times.
The revised valuation reflects weaker near-term return on equity, higher credit cost uncertainty and a delayed earnings recovery, despite progress in Affin's transformation through loan growth, resilient NIM and stronger fee income.
The firm said the risk-reward profile had shifted to the downside following two consecutive quarters of elevated provisions.
A further re-rating would depend on clearer evidence that credit costs have peaked, retail asset quality is stabilising and NCC is returning to normalised levels below 30 basis points.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HLIB maintains 'Buy' call on CIMB, RM8.70 target
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd Research (HLIB Research) maintained its "Buy" recommendation on CIMB Group Holdings Bhd, with a target price of RM8.70, compared with the stock's current price of RM7.95.
The target price implies an upside of about 9.4 per cent from its current level.
The research house said the recommendation followed steady second-quarter earnings from CIMB Group's Indonesian subsidiary, CIMB Niaga.
In a note, HLIB Research said CIMB Niaga's operations remained resilient, supported by stronger loan growth and broad-based non-interest income growth.
"CIMB Niaga's second-quarter (2Q26) core earnings fell 5.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) but increased 1.3 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in line with expectations.
"Loan growth accelerated to 6.6 per cent YoY, while asset quality improved markedly with gross impaired loans falling to 1.55 per cent," it said.
The research house said stronger corporate banking growth and improved loan demand across segments supported the acceleration in loan growth.
However, it remained cautious about elevated funding and credit costs, which could cap near-term improvements in return on equity.
CIMB Niaga's total revenue was broadly flat QoQ, as a 4.3 per cent decline in non-interest income offset a 3.5 per cent increase in net interest income.
The decline in non-interest income was mainly due to weaker treasury gains and fee income, while revenue grew 7.1 per cent YoY.
This was driven by a 21.2 per cent increase in non-interest income, supported by broad-based growth across income streams.
"Despite positive jaws, with revenue growth outpacing operating expenditure growth, net profit rose just 1.3 per cent, as a sharp increase in provisions more than offset the benefit from a lower effective tax rate," HLIB Research said.
For the first half, total income rose 6.7 per cent, supported by a 25.1 per cent increase in non-interest income.
However, higher operating expenses and provisions weighed on overall profitability during the period.
Deposit growth also improved to 2.8 per cent YoY, supported by stronger current account and savings account inflows, partly offset by lower time deposits.
HLIB Research said asset quality improved significantly, with CIMB Niaga's gross impaired loan ratio falling to 1.55 per cent from 2.82 per cent in 1Q26.
"Encouragingly, underlying asset quality remains intact, with gross impaired loan and loan-at-risk trends improving, backed by comfortable capital and liquidity buffers," it said.
Looking ahead, HLIB Research remained cautiously optimistic about CIMB Niaga's underlying franchise, citing above-guidance loan expansion and growing traction in recurring fee income.
Nevertheless, it cautioned that deposit competition, elevated funding costs and higher credit costs could limit near-term earnings growth and return on equity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six Johor students secure places at top global universities
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Six Johor students secured places at the world's leading universities after excelling in their A-Level examinations under the state's flagship Biasiswa Orang Muda Johor (BOMJ).
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the six scholars, from BOMJ's second cohort, would pursue studies in fields including robotics and artificial intelligence, biochemical engineering, chemical engineering and computer science.
Four have secured places at University College London (UCL), while another will study at the University of Manchester and one at the University of Pennsylvania.
"Their success is a source of pride for Johor and reflects the potential of our young people to compete at the highest level globally," Onn Hafiz said in a Facebook post.
At UCL, Amber Poi, who scored four A*s, will pursue Sustainable Built Environment, Energy and Resources.
Faiq Fathullah Mohd Yazid and Nur Maryam Norazam, who both scored three As and one A*, will study Robotics and Artificial Intelligence and Biochemical Engineering respectively.
Nurul Hidayah Norazam, who obtained two As and two A*s, will pursue Chemical Engineering at UCL.
T. Hemaraj, who scored three As and one A*, will also study Chemical Engineering at the University of Manchester.
Tan Wen Bin, who scored three As and one A*, will read Computer Science at the University of Pennsylvania, an Ivy League university in the United States.
The state government allocated RM1.75 million for BOMJ in 2025, with the scheme aimed at enabling academically outstanding students to pursue studies at top universities worldwide.
Onn Hafiz said the state hoped the scholars would eventually bring home the knowledge, expertise and international networks gained overseas to contribute to Johor's development.
"Insya-Allah, they will return not only with knowledge, but also experience and global networks that can help drive Johor's progress in the future," he said.
The latest cohort follows the success of earlier BOMJ recipients who secured places at institutions including Columbia University and Imperial College London, reinforcing the programme's ambition to place Johor students on the global academic map.

Title: Foreign buyers' exit from Malaysian stocks continues for second consecutive week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign institutions extended their net selling streak on Bursa Malaysia to two consecutive weeks, recording RM623.6 million in net outflows in the week ended August 14, according to MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB).
In its fund flow report, MBSB IB said foreign institutions were net sellers on all five trading days, with the highest outflow recorded on Friday at RM181.3 million, followed by Tuesday at RM171.4 million.
The transportation and logistics sector recorded the highest net foreign inflow at RM103.8 million, followed by telecommunication and media at RM34.9 million and energy at RM19.7 million.
Meanwhile, financial services recorded the largest net foreign outflow at RM469.3 million, followed by industrial products and services at RM121.2 million and consumer products and services at RM89.6 million.
Foreign institutions bought RM77 million more of Westports Holdings Bhd during the week to Aug 14 than they sold, followed by Axiata Group Bhd and MTT Shipping and Logistics Bhd which saw net foreign inflows of RM54.7 million and RM21.5 million respectively.
Meanwhile, Malayan Banking Bhd had the biggest net foreign outflows during the week, at RM293.8 million, followed by AMMB Holdings Bhd at RM114.6 million and Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd at RM104.2 million.
Local institutions extended their net buying streak to three consecutive weeks, recording RM355.5 million in net inflows.
Retail investors also returned as net buyers after two consecutive weeks of net selling, recording RM268.1 million in net inflows.
MBSB IB said average daily trading volume declined across all investor groups, with retail investors recording a 1.1 per cent decrease, local institutions 10.9 per cent and foreign institutions 3.7 per cent

Title: Analysts raise Malaysia growth outlook after Q2 GDP surge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economy grew by a stronger-than-expected 6.0 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in the second quarter of 2026 (FY26), prompting two investment banks to raise their full-year growth forecasts.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) revised its 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast to 5.3 per cent from 4.7 per cent previously, while Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) raised its projection to 5.4 per cent from 4.6 per cent.
Both research houses said the robust Q2 FY26 performance, which accelerated from 5.4 per cent in the first quarter, underscored the resilience of domestic demand and improving external activity, providing a stronger foundation for growth in the second half of the year.
HLIB Research said Q2 FY26 GDP growth slightly exceeded its 5.9 per cent forecast, as well as the Statistics Department's advance estimate and consensus median forecast of 5.8 per cent.
PublicInvest said growth was "relatively broad-based", supported by household spending, investment and stronger external demand.
"Domestic demand remained supportive, with household spending sustained by steady income growth, favourable labour market conditions and ongoing policy support.
"External demand provided a stronger lift with exports accelerating on continued electrical and electronics (E&E) strength, firmer services exports and a rebound in liquefied natural gas and non-E&E manufactured shipments," it said.
HLIB said private consumption remained the key growth engine, rising 4.8 per cent in Q2 FY26 from 4.7 per cent in Q1 FY26.
Public consumption also accelerated to 7.6 per cent from 4.1 per cent, while public investment increased to 6.3 per cent from 5.3 per cent.
PublicInvest said household spending and public expenditure continued to support domestic demand, although private investment moderated to 4.3 per cent from 7.8 per cent.
On the supply side, manufacturing growth accelerated to 7.3 per cent from 5.9 per cent, driven mainly by export-orientated industries, particularly E&E, amid robust artificial intelligence-related demand.
Services growth also improved to 5.9 per cent from 5.6 per cent, while mining rebounded sharply to 9.2 per cent from a 2.1 per cent contraction in 1Q26.
PublicInvest said the mining recovery was supported by stronger natural gas production and favourable base effects, while agriculture contracted 3.7 per cent from 2.6 per cent growth previously, as oil palm production normalised following strong yields in 2025.
HLIB Research said the Malaysian economy demonstrated resilience against external shocks, with first-half 2026 GDP growth reaching 5.7 per cent.
"Going forward, we expect export activity and sustained domestic demand to support growth ahead, though 2H26 is likely to moderate due to strong 2H25 growth," it said.
PublicInvest also expects growth to remain relatively firm in the second half, forecasting around 5.1 per cent YoY supported by resilient domestic demand, continued investment execution and sustained technology-related activity.
However, both research firms highlighted external risks, including the Middle East conflict, global trade uncertainties and US trade measures.
PublicInvest said the unusually strong external contribution in 2Q26 was unlikely to be repeated as front-loading effects fade and global trade growth softens.
Both research firms maintained expectations for Bank Negara to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent through the second half of 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Starting them young on healthy gut habits
Article:
TAIPING: Healthy gut habits should be nurtured from a young age as the digestive system plays a crucial role in supporting overall health, beyond simply aiding digestion.
This was the key message delivered during the "A Healthier Gut Starts Young, Starts Within" programme jointly organised by Yakult Malaysia and Columbia Asia Hospital Taiping at Hua Lian High School here.
The programme brought together more than 100 parents and children to raise awareness of digestive wellness while encouraging families to adopt healthier lifestyle habits from a young age.
Yakult (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd's Public Relations and Science Division associate director Mazlyn Mena Mustapha said awareness of gut health among Malaysians remained relatively low, partly because the gut was an aspect of health that could not be physically seen.
"In fact, maintaining a balance of bacteria in the gut is very important for our overall health."
Mazlyn said the gut is home to a natural community of bacteria, comprising both beneficial and less beneficial bacteria, and maintaining a healthy balance between them was essential.
She said gut health is also closely linked to the body's immune system, with about 80 per cent of the immune system located in the gut.
"So, when we keep our gut healthy, it not only helps with digestion, but also strengthens the immune system and has a significant impact on our overall health."
Mazlyn said Yakult Malaysia is taking its health awareness campaign to communities nationwide through programmes tailored to the needs of different age groups.
"We want to increase awareness by organising health awareness events like this across the country. However, we focus on specific communities and bring these programmes directly to them."
She said similar programmes had previously been held in Negri Sembilan, Johor Baru and Sarawak, with upcoming programmes planned in Kedah and the East Coast.
On when parents should start paying attention to their children's gut health, Mazlyn said it could begin when babies started consuming food other than breast milk.
She said babies receive beneficial bacteria from their mothers, including through breastfeeding.
"Once the baby starts weaning and eating foods other than breast milk, we can start paying attention to maintaining the balance of bacteria in the gut."
Mazlyn said probiotic drinks could also be introduced at that stage, although parents should start with small amounts and gradually increase the intake while monitoring their children's bowel movements.
She said Yakult's efforts to promote gut health extended beyond children, with the company also conducting health awareness programmes for senior citizens.
She said continued community outreach was important to help Malaysians understand that taking care of their gut was not merely about preventing digestive problems, but was an important part of maintaining overall health throughout life.
The programme also featured educational health talks, free health screenings, a children's colouring contest and an interactive, hands-on yoghurt bowl-making workshop.
A dedicated wellness zone also provided families with complimentary screenings and consultations from Columbia Asia Hospital Taiping, 20dB Hearing Sdn Bhd, YES Rehab Sdn Bhd, MU Optic, Klinik Pergigian Taiping.

Title: DAP sets Anwar year-end deadline for AG-PP separation, PM term limit bills
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been given until year-end to ensure key institutional reforms, including separating the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor and limiting the prime minister's tenure to two terms, are passed.
DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo said the party's decision to remain in the Federal Government must now be followed by concrete action on its core reform agenda.
"I urge Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to take immediate action to realise these reforms. There must be clear, unyielding timelines set for foundational institutional reforms," he said in a statement today.
Gobind, who is also Digital Minister, said the groundwork had already been laid, with the AG-PP separation Bill and proposed two-term limit for prime ministers already prepared.
He also called for amendments to the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act (Sosma) and the Peaceful Assembly Act to be finalised and tabled without further delay.
He said a ministerial statement on Sosma amendments had been tabled in Parliament in February last year, while amendments to the Peaceful Assembly Act had been under discussion for months.
Gobind also proposed a special parliamentary sitting or additional Dewan Rakyat sitting days to allow the reform Bills to be debated and passed, similar to the recent special sitting on the Royal Commission of Inquiry report on Tabung Haji.
"The government had acted with speed by holding a special parliamentary session for the RCI report on Tabung Haji.
"A similar route ought to be taken for these crucial reform Bills, or additional sitting days must be added to the upcoming Dewan Rakyat session specifically dedicated to these," he said.
Gobind said DAP remained committed to ensuring the reforms were carried through without further delay.
"We should look towards getting these Bills passed before the end of this year," he said.
DAP delegates voted overwhelmingly on Aug 16
to remain in the unity government, with 88 per cent choosing to stay for the remainder of the parliamentary term.
A total of 1,857 delegates voted to remain, while 242 voted to leave.
The result was announced by national congress chairman Chua Kee Chin at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre.
Of the 2,230 delegates who attended, 2,106 ballot papers were issued and returned, with 2,099 valid votes and seven spoiled ballots.

Title: Father breaks down in court as four charged with son's murder
Article:
BATU PAHAT: The father of murdered businessman Low Kai Xian broke down in tears in court today as four men were charged with killing his son.
The victim's body was found wrapped in a net and dumped into a river earlier this month.
The man, in his 60s, arrived at the magistrate's court visibly grief-stricken, walking slowly into the courtroom with the support of family members.
However, his composure gave way when the murder charge was read out.
Tears streamed down his face as he listened to the proceedings involving his 39-year-old son.
The family's lawyer, Chuah Shyue Chien, said the father was overwhelmed by grief as he confronted the reality of what had happened to his son.
"He is sad and broke down in tears. The family told us that they leave it entirely to the court to decide the fate of those accused of killing their son," he said when met outside the court.
The four accused — lorry driver Yogesvaran Subramaniam, 40; lorry attendants Lim Yong Ming, 26, and Achuthan Nagarajan, 32; and used-car dealer How Han Wei, 33 — were charged with murder before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
All four nodded after the charge was read to them.
They face the
death penalty
upon conviction.
The proceedings drew Low's grieving family to court as early as 7.45am, with several relatives waiting outside in the hope of seeing the four accused face the court.
They remained silent when approached by reporters and later left the court without speaking to the media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CAP calls for prosecution of 'Malaysian Epstein Class' over Tabung Haji scandal
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has called for sweeping prosecutions after the Tabung Haji (TH) Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) exposed serious governance and accounting failures.
CAP president Mohideen Abdul Kader described those responsible as a "Malaysian Epstein Class", alleging that a network of political, professional, regulatory and institutional figures enabled the mismanagement of depositors' funds.
The characterisation was made by CAP in a statement following the declassification of the RCI report into TH, which examined the institution's management between 2014 and 2020.
It was reported that a shipping company chief executive officer with a Datuk title was among seven people detained by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) so far to assist investigations into
the scandal
.
Also detained were a company director and a former company director, both holding Datuk and Datuk Seri titles respectively, as well as four former senior TH management officers.
Mohideen said the scandal should not be reduced to the actions of a handful of individuals, arguing that the RCI findings pointed to wider institutional failures and a culture that allowed questionable practices to continue.
The 211-page RCI report found that TH should have recorded a RM1.4 billion net loss instead of a RM3.4 billion profit in 2017 if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards had been fully applied.
It also found that TH had been operating with an asset-liability deficit since 2014, while impairment losses on investments were not fully recognised.
High hibah payments between 2014 and 2017 further weakened the institution's reserves.
"The findings raised questions over the roles played by religious administrators, accountants, lawyers, regulators, government officials and political leaders in overseeing the institution," he added.
Mohideen called on Parliament to issue a bipartisan censure and urged authorities to investigate every individual who may have breached fiduciary or legal duties, rather than focusing only on senior figureheads.
He specifically called on the Royal Malaysia Police, MACC and Attorney-General's Chambers to pursue those implicated by evidence from the RCI report.
CAP also urged the authorities to recover any ill-gotten assets and impose the full penalties available under Malaysian law.
"The scandal has damaged public confidence in an institution established to manage the savings of Muslims preparing for the Hajj pilgrimage," he stressed.
The Cabinet declassified the RCI report on July 29, with the full document, recommendations and inquiry proceedings subsequently made public.
A special Dewan Rakyat sitting was also held to debate the findings.
Mohideen said the episode should serve as a warning that political influence and weak oversight must never be allowed to compromise the management of public and religious funds.

Title: 1,040 seized plant saplings found infested with pests, diseases
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: A total of 1,040 plant saplings seized by the General Operations Force (GOF) in two operations here were found to be infested with pests or diseases and will be destroyed.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the affected saplings were among 5,770 seized from two lorries yesterday.
He said all the seized plants were handed over to the Kelantan Agriculture Department for further action, with the affected saplings to be disposed of through crushing and burial.
"The 1,040 saplings from both seizures were found to contain pests or diseases and will be disposed of by the Agriculture Department through crushing and burial," he said.
The seizures, involving plants worth RM217,500, were made by the Strike Force team of the GOF Seventh Battalion in two separate operations in Rantau Panjang.
In the first case, he said the team stopped a lorry near the Rantau Panjang fire and rescue station after spotting it being driven suspiciously at 1pm.
"Checks on the 23-year-old driver and the lorry led to the discovery of various types of plant saplings.
"The driver failed to produce satisfactory documents for the plants, prompting police to detain him and seize the lorry and its contents," he said.
He said the seizure comprised 60 kenanga plants, 80 batik kaffir lime saplings and 250 ixora saplings, among others.
Radzi said the lorry was valued at RM150,000, while the plants were estimated to be worth RM67,500.
In the second seizure, he said the team stopped an Isuzu lorry near a petrol station in Rantau Panjang at 2pm.
Checks found 4,000 plant saplings, including 600 rhu, 600 cherry, 500 tecoma, 500 keranji biji and 500 bunga tanjung saplings.
"The 35-year-old driver, who was also unable to produce satisfactory documents, was detained and the lorry and plants seized.
"The lorry was valued at RM150,000, while the plants were estimated to be worth RM235,000," he said.
Radzi said both cases were investigated under Section 6 of the Plant Quarantine Act 1976.
Preliminary investigations found that both drivers had been hired to collect the plants from an illegal jetty and deliver them to a nursery in Rantau Panjang.
"Each driver was paid RM150 for the transportation service. Checks also found that both lorry drivers have no previous records," he said.

Title: Johor targets 200,000 jobs from quality investments by 2030
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor is prioritising investments that create high-paying jobs, develop local talent and strengthen local businesses, rather than simply pursuing headline investment figures.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said this was the focus of his meeting with Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today, which discussed the direction of investment and industrial development in the state.
"Johor's eight per cent Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in 2025, which is the highest recorded among states in the country, has strengthened confidence in the state's economic trajectory.
"However, our measure of success is not only the amount of investment brought in, but also how far these investments can create quality and high-income jobs, develop local talent and directly benefit Bangsa Johor," he said in a Facebook post today.
Onn Hafiz said investments entering Johor must generate wider economic spillovers, particularly by creating opportunities for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), developing local vendors and companies, and strengthening domestic supply chains.
He said the state government, through Invest Johor and the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA), would work closely with the Federal Government to attract more quality investments and high-value projects.
"Through close cooperation between the state government, Invest Johor and MIDA, with the continued support of the federal government, we are targeting more quality investments and high-value projects in Johor," he said.
The effort aims to create more than 200,000 new job opportunities for Bangsa Johor and Malaysians by 2030.
Onn Hafiz said Johor was poised to remain a key engine of economic growth, driven by its strategic location, industrial base and growing investment ecosystem.
He said development must translate into tangible benefits for the people, particularly through better employment opportunities and stronger participation by local businesses.
"The benefits of development must return to the people," he said, adding that Johor's economic ambitions must go beyond investment figures.
The push comes as Johor positions itself as a key growth hub under the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, with the state seeking to attract investments while ensuring local businesses and workers benefit from the economic opportunities.

Title: Malaysia's current account surplus to remain firm at 2.1pct of GDP in 2026 – Kenanga IB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd (Kenanga IB) expects Malaysia's 2026 current account to remain firmly in surplus, maintaining a forecast at 2.1 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), compared with 1.6 per cent in 2025.
In a note today, the investment bank said Malaysia's external position should remain resilient despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainties from the conflict in Middle East.
"Costlier energy and a softer global demand could crimp parts of world trade, but Malaysia's exposure is cushioned by the electrical and electronics (E&E) and artificial intelligence (AI) upcycle, particularly semiconductors, servers and data-centre infrastructure.
"The (positive) second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026) GDP print supports this view, with growth stepping up to 6.0 per cent (Q1 2026: 5.4 per cent), while a rebound in liquefied natural gas (LNG) and non-E&E shipments adds further breadth," it said.
Kenanga IB also said hyperscaler capital expenditure and inventory normalisation across advanced economies should keep Malaysia's export demand supported through 2026, while tourism and digital-infrastructure spending should lift services exports.
"A firmer ringgit could nudge imports higher, and energy costs remain a swing factor, but we expect the external balance to stay comfortably in surplus," it said.
On Friday, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) announced that Malaysia's current account balance recorded a surplus of RM10.8 billion in Q2 2026, supported by a substantial increase in the goods surplus to RM40.7 billion.
DOSM said the surplus cushioned the decline in the services account, which turned to a deficit of RM0.7 billion from a surplus of RM6.4 billion in Q1 2026.
Meanwhile, Bank Negara Malaysia also announced that Malaysia's economy expanded by 6.0 per cent in Q2 2026, surpassing DOSM's advance estimate of 5.8 per cent, driven by sustained domestic demand and robust export performance.

Title: Search for Indonesia quake victims underway on Independence Day
Article:
ENDE: Rescuers in eastern Indonesia will comb through collapsed buildings on Monday to find anyone who might still be trapped under rubble after a deadly quake that killed at least 53 people, as the country marks its Independence Day reeling from the impact of fresh tremors.
Saturday's disaster in the province of East Nusa Tenggara was the country's deadliest since a 2022 quake killed hundreds in West Java. The official death toll was at 53 as of late Sunday.
The quake also caused landslides and blocked roads across Indonesia's southernmost province, including the regions of Sikka and Manggarai.
Thousands were evacuated, with many sheltering in tents outdoors and afraid to return to their homes due to fears of aftershocks.
There were nearly 1,600 aftershocks in the province as of Monday, local media reported the geophysics agency chief as saying. The agency reported a 5.6-magnitude quake in Nagekeo region, near the initial epicentre, on Monday morning.
In the parking lot of a damaged health centre littered with tents and hospital beds in a village close to the quake-affected Ende region, Firmus Woge, a 64-year-old farmer, was being treated for his asthma, aggravated by the panic setting in as the buildings around him continued to rattle.
He said he had difficulty breathing overnight. Though better on Monday morning, the fresh aftershocks again took his breath away.
"I felt better last night and this morning but it's getting worse again after this morning's quake," he said, gasping for breath.
SEARCH TO CONTINUE
The search will continue on Monday, authorities said. Fathur Rahman, chief at the rescue office in Maumere, Sikka's capital, told Reuters on Monday the search will focus on aerial monitoring for anyone missing.
[[nid:1512852]]
Rescuers will use an extrication device and a helicopter, Fathur said, adding there were no reports of people missing and no challenges hampering the search.
Authorities readied planes to deliver aid such as food and tents, the chief of the country's disaster mitigation agency Suharyanto said late on Sunday. The quake damaged around 500 homes, he said.
Indonesia will also build an emergency field hospital in several areas, said Benjamin Paulus Octavianus, the country's deputy health minister.
Neurosurgeons and orthopaedic surgeons are needed to treat head trauma and broken bones, Benjamin said.
'I DON'T THINK ABOUT THAT ANYMORE'
In Jakarta, about 1,500 km (930 miles) west of the disaster zone, President Prabowo Subianto is expected on Monday to preside over celebrations marking Indonesia's independence from Japanese rule in 1945.
Residents fleeing from an Ende village in fear of tsunamis brought their clothes and mattresses to higher ground.
Asked about how he felt about the Independence Day celebrations, one resident, Gervas, 42, said: "I don't think about that anymore … I just think about the safety of my wife and 4-year-old twins."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mara Corp ex-CEO fails to overturn RM3.4mil court order
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Majlis Amanah Rakyat Corporation (Mara Corp) former chief executive officer Datuk Badlisyah Abdul Ghani has failed in his bid to overturn a court order requiring him to pay RM3.4 million to the company for breaching his contractual, fiduciary and statutory duties.
A three-member Court of Appeal panel, led by Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, upheld the High Court's decision against Badlisyah, finding no reason to interfere with the lower court's findings.
The other members of the panel were Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid and Datuk Ahmad Fairuz Zainol Abidin.
On May 20, 2024, the High Court ordered Badlisyah to pay Mara Corp RM3,468,215.42 and indemnify the company against expenses arising from industrial relations claims involving former employees.
Badlisyah was appointed Mara Corp chief executive officer on Sept 8, 2020, but was suspended from duty on Nov 19 that year before being terminated with effect from Jan 12, 2021.
The case centred on two main issues — Badlisyah's hiring of 25 employees without the required approval from the board of directors and his misrepresentation to the Board Nomination and Remuneration Committee (BNRC) concerning four employees.
Twelve of the employees were appointed to senior director positions, which the court found were beyond Badlisyah's authority.
Court questions hiring of 25 employees
Ahmad Kamal, who wrote the grounds of judgment dated Aug 12, said the hiring of 25 employees within a short period raised serious concerns.
"The short span of two months of hiring the 25 employees within just two weeks from commencement of the appellant's employment on Sept 8, 2020, sparks grave suspicion.
"It clearly shows the appellant could not have exercised his mind appropriately when dealing with the same.
"The timing, haste and surreptitious manner of the hiring of 25 employees could not have been made within the reasonable scope of carrying on the business of Mara in good faith," he said.
The court said the 25 appointments cost the company about RM9.4 million a year in salaries, noting that Mara Corp's approved emolument budget for 2020 was only RM1.799 million.
It also found that Badlisyah had exceeded his authority by hiring or extending the employment of the 25 employees without prior recommendation from the BNRC and approval from the board.
Kamal agreed with the High Court that Badlisyah had wrongly approved an internal memo that effectively expanded his authority to appoint senior directors.
He said Badlisyah's attempt to expand his authority through an internal memo was invalid, as the company's Limits of Authority could only be amended by the board.
Court upholds misrepresentation finding
The court also upheld the finding that Badlisyah had misrepresented the status of four employees during a BNRC meeting on Nov 2, 2020.
During the meeting, he proposed the four employees for senior positions and told the committee that they were "ready to join Mara Corp".
However, the court found that the four had already been engaged by Mara Corp, even though the positions were still being considered by the BNRC and had yet to receive board approval.
The Court of Appeal also ordered Badlisyah to pay RM50,000 in costs to Mara Corp.
Lawyers Jack S'ng, Chng Keng Lung, Irene Wong and Sarah Tham appeared for the company, while Badlisyah was unrepresented.

Title: Strengthen cycling regulations to protect all road users
Article:
LETTER:
The authorities must urgently introduce clearer guidelines, regulations and stronger enforcement on cycling activities on main roads and expressways to ensure the safety of cyclists and all other road users.
Cycling is a healthy and beneficial sporting activity and should be encouraged. However, with its growing popularity, proper safety guidelines and facilities are needed.
Cycling on busy main roads can pose dangers not only to cyclists but also to motorists, especially due to the significant difference in speed.
It can lead to sudden braking, dangerous overtaking and traffic congestion, particularly on narrow and heavily congested roads.
Many road users also feel frustrated when cyclists occupy busy roads during peak traffic hours, further adding to an already difficult journey.
The lack of proper and connected cycling facilities has resulted in many cyclists turning to public roads, creating an increasing challenge that must be addressed.
Publicly available statistics have shown that more than 100 cyclists were killed annually in certain reported years.
While comprehensive national data on all cycling-related accidents is not consistently available, these fatalities clearly show that cyclist safety remains a serious concern.
Malaysia should learn from the Netherlands and Denmark, where cycling is supported through proper infrastructure, including dedicated and safer cycling lanes separated from high-speed traffic.
In many developed countries, cyclists are also prohibited from using motorways and designated high-speed roads, while suitable cycling routes are provided.
Malaysia must adopt a balanced approach.
The government should strictly enforce the prohibition of cycling on expressways and designated high-speed highways, while developing proper cycling tracks and facilities in cities and areas where cycling activities are popular.
The existing laws do not appear to fully address the growing challenges arising from the increasing number of cyclists on Malaysian roads.
Any new regulations and enforcement must not be seen as an attempt to discourage cycling, but rather as an effort to protect cyclists, motorists, motorcyclists, pedestrians and all other road users.
We must encourage a healthy lifestyle, but safety must always come first.
Proper regulations, effective enforcement and adequate cycling infrastructure are urgently needed to ensure that Malaysian roads are safer for everyone.
JEYARATNAM MANIUM @ AJAAY
PPP Communication Chief
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nanta: Four strategies identified to tackle contractor fraud
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Four strategies have been identified to tackle fraud involving registered and unregistered contractors, with victims suffering losses of up to hundreds of thousands of ringgit.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi acknowledged that protecting homeowners required more than simply verifying whether a contractor was registered with the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB).
He said other measures were needed, including stronger enforcement, greater transparency of information, consumer education and inter-agency cooperation.
Nanta said CIDB received 3,201 complaints between 2018 and 2025 involving contractors engaged in house construction and renovation, with most cases involving breaches of contractual agreements.
"On average, CIDB receives about 600 complaints a year involving such issues. In 2024 alone, 564 complaints were recorded, while 367 complaints had been received as of October last year.
"Among the complaints were breaches of contractual agreements, unsatisfactory construction quality, unregistered contractors, safety issues, outstanding payments and failure to comply with building material standards," he told Berita Harian.
He said the breakdown of cases up to October 2025 included 130 involving breaches of contract, 86 related to construction quality and 50 involving unregistered contractors.
"However, we also acknowledge that the number of complaints received by CIDB does not reflect the full extent of the problem, as some cases are reported directly to the Tribunal for Consumer Claims Malaysia, police, elected representatives or are only highlighted on social media."
To address the issue, he said CIDB had introduced the Jom Bina Sempurna programme to raise homeowners' awareness of the construction and renovation process, enabling them to choose contractors carefully, use contracts, monitor work and make payments based on actual project progress.
Launched in 2025, Jom Bina Sempurna is a national awareness programme aimed at helping homeowners and contractors ensure construction and renovation work is carried out properly, safely and according to the required standards.
It was reported on Aug 9 that fraud involving certain contractors remained an ongoing problem, with cases continuing to surface through various channels, including social media.
Some homeowners have not only fallen victim to unregistered contractors but have also been cheated by registered contractors, suffering losses of hundreds of thousands of ringgit after failing to receive services commensurate with the payments made.
Nanta said CIDB had clear enforcement powers against contractors who violated the CIDB Act or registration requirements.
"These include conducting investigations, issuing compounds, taking action against registrations, imposing restrictions in the system and prosecution, depending on the nature of the offence."
As for unregistered contractors, he said carrying out construction work without registration was an offence punishable by a fine of between RM10,000 and RM100,000 upon conviction under Section 29 of the CIDB Act.
"CIDB can also issue notices ordering construction work to be stopped under Section 30. However, it must be made clear that when a complaint involves elements of fraud, forgery or a criminal offence, it must be referred to the enforcement agency with criminal jurisdiction."
Nanta added that a major challenge in detecting unregistered contractors was that they operated outside the official registration system, making early monitoring difficult and increasing risks for homeowners.
"Therefore, homeowners need to ensure that the contractor they appoint is properly registered before work begins.
"Using unregistered contractors exposes homeowners to the risk of abandoned projects, poor workmanship, lack of work guarantees, liability issues and difficulty obtaining redress when disputes arise."
Based on previous enforcement operations, he said some
reasons contractors remained unregistered included a lack of awareness of registration requirements, financial and company documentation problems, as well as reliance on the registration of main contractors or other companies.s

Title: Air quality improves, Johan Setia still records unhealthy API
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality nationwide improved as at 10 am today compared with last night, with only Johan Setia, Selangor recording an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading.
The area recorded an API reading of 151, which falls within the unhealthy category, according to the data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal.
Meanwhile, 58 areas recorded moderate API readings of between 51 and 100, while another eight areas recorded good air quality with readings below 50.
An API reading of between zero and 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are classified as hazardous.
The API data are updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — BERNAMA

Title: Four charged with murder of businessman found in river [WATCH]
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Four men were charged in the Magistrate's Court today with murdering a businessman whose body was found wrapped in a net and floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, on Aug 3.
The accused are lorry driver Yogesvaran Subramaniam, 40; lorry attendants Lim Yong Ming, 26, and Achuthan Nagarajan, 32; and used-car dealer How Han Wei, 33.
The four merely nodded after the charge was read before Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
No plea was recorded as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The four were jointly charged with murdering Low Kai Xian, 39, between an eatery in Jalan Emas Putih, Taman Sri Skudai, Johor Baru, and Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, between 2.35pm on July 29 and 12.30pm on Aug 3.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read with Section 34, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, with not less than 12 strokes of whipping if the death penalty is not imposed, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Firdaus Ruslan appeared for the prosecution, while all four accused were unrepresented.
The prosecution sought a new mention date pending completion of the post-mortem, DNA, closed-circuit television (CCTV) and mobile phone forensic reports.
No bail was offered.
The court allowed the application and fixed Oct 14 for mention pending the completion of the reports.
Low was reported missing by his family on July 29 after they were unable to contact him. His family later found only his multipurpose vehicle (MPV) in Johor Baru.
Police subsequently received information from a member of the public at 12.30pm on Aug 3 about a
body found in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong.
Initial investigations found that the victim's hands and legs had been bound with adhesive tape, while injuries were found on his waist and arms.
The body had been wrapped and secured in a net, with five pieces of stone found inside.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jason Arday: UK academic who died amid plagiarism storm
Article:
JASON Arday, the ex-Cambridge professor found dead amid a growing furore over claims of academic plagiarism and personal life embellishments, rose from humble roots in Britain to be hailed as an academic superstar.
Boasting a backstory of remarkable achievement despite childhood autism and other developmental disorders, by the time of his death on Friday Arday was at the epicentre of intense controversy. He was 41.
Cambridge University's youngest black professor when appointed in March 2023 aged 37, he quickly emerged from relative obscurity to a prominent figure known outside academia.
That skyrocketed in recent weeks, as plagiarism allegations and unrelenting scrutiny of other seemingly outlandish claims played out within the context of the West's so-called culture wars.
Arday resigned from his Cambridge roles earlier this month after the university announced internal probes.
Detractors have criticised the university for the appointment, claiming he unfairly benefited from diversity, equality and inclusion (DEI) policies.
But Arday, his family and his supporters have alleged a racist "campaign of sustained abuse" and media witchhunt.
Married since 2014, he is survived by two children.
Jason Atta Kwei Arday was born in May 1985 in south London, one of four brothers, to parents originally from Ghana.
The midwife who delivered him told his mum "he's going to do something special", Arday wrote in a memoir being published this month.
His book also notes another prophecy, delivered some two decades later by an aid worker during a relief mission he joined in Brazil.
"You're destined to do great things, but I also believe you're destined for very sad and difficult things as well," Arday recalled her saying.
The autobiography recounts doctors diagnosing him with autism and global developmental delay – a term applied to under-fives with issues around motor skills and speech.
[[nid:1512771]]
Doctors branded him "a lost cause" and therapists warned he would require lifelong support, he wrote.
He credited his mental health nurse mum – an anti-racism activist whom he always called Giff – with helping defy the predictions, in part using music to aid his linguistic understanding.
Arday writes that he was non-verbal until 11 after "thousands of hours" of speech therapy.
Some of his childhood claims have been disputed, with at least two former schoolmates telling The Guardian they recalled him speaking during this period.
But others have spoken up in support.
"The coverage about him being a fantasist and a liar that does not ring true with the human that I know and loved," childhood friend Mike Freeman told Sky News.
Arday did not read or write until he was 18, according to his biography on Cambridge's website.
He gained just two school-level qualifications – in Physical Education (PE) and textiles.
After earning a vocational qualification in sport and development, he became a PE teacher before launching his academic career.
He subsequently earned PE and education-related university degrees before earning a PhD from Liverpool John Moores University.
While studying for his PhD, he wrote a set of goals on a bedroom wall. "One of these read: 'One day I will work at Oxford or Cambridge'," he wrote.
Arday fulfilled that dream within a decade, after academic roles at Roehampton, Durham and Glasgow universities, becoming a sociology of education professor at Cambridge.
He was commended by Cambridge as a "highly respected scholar of race, inequality and education."
But around this time, plagiarism concerns first surfaced.
[[nid:1512770]]
David Harris, a British academic who published a 2024 critique of critical race theory, is said to have contacted Arday and Cambridge with claims.
Arday reportedly lodged a harassment complaint against Harris with police.
Two years later, a Times Higher Education reporter contacted Arday with similar allegations but abandoned the story after receiving a letter from a leading defamation law firm on behalf of Arday, The Times said.
Then in July Nathan Cofnas, a US academic and self-defined "race realist" – whose Cambridge research affiliation ended in 2024 amid racism accusations – published further plagiarism claims.
The Telegraph newspaper followed up, alleging dozens of passages in Arday's PhD had been copied from another earlier thesis.
Meanwhile some of his claimed accomplishments, around marathon-running and fundraising, as well as over the alleged abuse he faced, have been disputed in newspaper probes.
Arday admitted making academic "mistakes" but said he was being falsely portrayed as a liar.
He told The Times some early academic errors were due to his autism, as he relied on using mimicry to understand information.
Arday has also insisted black academics face racially motivated systemic targeting, alleging conservative "activists" on both sides of the Atlantic were using a "playbook" to discredit them, according to reports.
"It's a disgrace and, quite frankly, evil," he reportedly told a conference.
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Asian shares mark time as Gulf war keeps oil prices up
Article:
SYDNEY: Asian shares drifted sideways on Monday while investors kept a wary eye on oil prices, which notched sizeable gains last week as the lack of progress towards ending the Iran war kept inflation risks tilted to the upside.
Progress towards peace talks and oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz remained halted. Iran on Saturday called on the US to accept defeat, while President Donald Trump urged Americans to accept higher gasoline prices while the conflict continues.
At least 11 people were killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon on Saturday, the Lebanese health ministry said, some of the deadliest in the weeks since the country agreed to a US-mediated peace framework with neighbouring Israel.
Brent crude was steady at US$88.50 a barrel after rising 6 per cent last week, while US crude slipped 0.3 per cent to US$82.12 a barrel, having gained 5.4 per cent last week.
"While there is still no resolution to the Iran/Hormuz impasse, our base case remains that oil prices will stay in a $70-$100 range with Iran preventing it going lower and the US moving to try and calm things down whenever it gets above $100," Shane Oliver, chief economist at AMP, said in a note.
"The risk remains that there will be no sustainable peace deal, the flow of oil out of the Middle East remains down 10%-15% on normal levels and that we will have to face higher oil prices as reserves run down."
On Monday, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was flat, while Japan's Nikkei edged 0.4 per cent higher. Australia's resources-heavy shares slipped 0.3 per cent.
South Korea's stock markets are closed on Monday for a public holiday. Trump has instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with the country.
All eyes are on the release of China's activity data for July on Monday after its exports boomed on robust global AI demand to support the world's second largest economy. Forecasts are centred on a slowdown in industrial output growth to 4.8 per cent, from 5.3 per cent previously, while retail sales likely rose 1.5 per cent.
For Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures rose 0.2 per cent. S&P 500 futures gained 0.1 per cent, having hit a record last week, while Nasdaq futures firmed 0.2 per cent.
The bullish run in stocks has been driven by diminishing risk that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month, which is now seen as a 69 per cent probability event after a slew of soft data.
US retail sales posted the first decline in nine months in July and consumer sentiment soured by more than expected, adding to soft inflation readings that took out the impetus for the Fed to hike immediately.
The main data point this week is the August S&P Purchasing Managers' Indices (PMIs) to see if the mid-year acceleration in US business activity would be sustained. Earnings are lighter this week but include Home Depot, Target and Walmart as investors scrutinise the strength of US consumers.
In bond markets, US Treasury yields slipped on Monday after finishing last week mixed. The two-year US Treasury yield fell 2 basis points to 4.156 per cent, having fallen 3 basis points last week to touch a seven-week low of 4.0977 per cent. Ten-year yields slipped 1 basis point to 4.684 per cent, after rising 4 basis points last week.
The soft run of data has weighed on the US dollar, with the euro up 0.1 per cent at US$1.1578, just off a two-month peak of US$1.1585. The dollar slipped 0.1 per cent on the yen to 159.15.
In commodity markets, gold held at US$4,381 an ounce, having climbed 0.8 per cent last week.
