Title: DAP delegates have spoken, respect their decision, Kon Yeow tells Rafizi over unity govt stance
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — DAP central executive committee member Chow Kon Yeow today told Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli to respect the party and its delegates’ decision to remain in the unity government.
Chow said this was a basic principle following Rafizi’s comments on the resolution adopted at DAP’s congress yesterday.
“We ask Rafizi to respect DAP and the decision of its delegates. That is the basic thing to do, isn’t it?” he told reporters after launching the public participation programme for the Draft Penang Structure Plan 2040 here.
Yesterday, Bersama leader Rafizi was reported saying that DAP’s decision to remain in the unity government was expected, claiming it was difficult for any political party that had “enjoyed” power to simply give it up.
Asked about claims that attendance at the DAP congress was below 50 per cent, Chow said the gathering remained valid as it had met the party’s quorum requirement.
He said at least 25 per cent of eligible delegates were required for the congress to proceed.
“We had more than 50 per cent and met the quorum requirement,” he said.
“Attendance at party elections is usually around 60 to 70 per cent, while voter turnout in a general election does not necessarily reach the full number either.
“So, does that mean our general election is invalid because only 65 per cent came out to vote? No,” he added.
On Rafizi’s remarks that Penang’s limited land supply had affected state revenue compared with states such as Johor, Chow said the state government had always planned for land development.
He said land acquisition and the opening up of land for development were ongoing for various purposes, including industrial use.
“The reclassification of rural areas as urban areas is also one method of rezoning land use in Penang,” he said.
“The state government maximises the use of existing land to ensure that development delivers the greatest impact for the state, taking into account Penang’s strengths and constraints,” he added.

Title: Penang’s undersea tunnel still on the map, draft plan keeps idea alive for 2040
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — The proposed undersea tunnel or third bridge linking Penang island to the mainland was included as an indicative proposal in the Draft Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (RSN Penang 2040), Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today.
He said the project remain in the draft plan as the agreement with the appointed company is still valid, although its eventual implementation would depend on development schedules.
“They are still there. The agreement is still valid and we have already awarded the tender to the company,” he told reporters after launching the publicity and public participation programme for the draft plan.
“Like many development areas and zones, they are shown only indicatively,” he said.
The third link, categorised as either an undersea tunnel or a bridge, was indicated in the draft plan as connecting Gurney Drive on the island to Bagan Ajam on the mainland.
He said the development areas and projects in the draft plan are indicative only as the implementation depends on the government of the day or sometimes, on the private sector in accordance with the designated development-control zones.
He said the draft RSN Penang 2040 should serve as a “compass” for the state’s development.
He said the draft plan gives clear direction on how Penang is developed, preserved and handed down to future generations.
“What we plan today will determine the face of Penang in 2040 and the generations after it, because Penang 2040 is not merely the state government’s vision; it is our shared future,” he said.
Chow also urged government departments and agencies to submit proposals for approved major projects to be included in the draft structure plan.
“It is important for us to include any proposal at the respective departmental level if approval has already been granted by the ministry to implement certain projects, especially major projects,” he said in his speech earlier.
“Provide this input during these public hearing sessions so that we can include these projects in RSN 2040,” he said.
“If there are plans that cannot be included, then when they are implemented, they will raise question marks among stakeholders, including the media, who will ask why this proposal is not in the RSN or in the local plan, for example,” he added.
Chow stressed that the draft was not a final or flawless document, and said the public could examine it, give feedback, submit proposals and challenge suggestions based on facts and public interest.
On Pulau Jerejak, he said the island is also included in the draft plan, but stressed that most of its land remains designated as a permanent forest reserve.
He said more than 80 acres of privately owned land are involved in the development proposals previously announced, while projects within the permanent forest reserve could only be considered for utilities or infrastructure.
“What was announced involves privately owned land, not the permanent forest reserve on Pulau Jerejak,” he said.
Asked whether the plan considered earthquake resilience and other disasters, Chow said disaster-related concerns had been given attention in the policies and development strategies proposed for the future.
Meanwhile, PLANMalaysia director-general Datuk Alias Rameli said the RSN Penang 2040 study was fully supported by a RM2 million allocation under the Fifth Rolling Plan of the 12th Malaysia Plan, with funding to continue under the First Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan.
He said the study was completed over 12 months, from April 2025 to April 2026.
The public participation programme will run for four weeks until September 19.
The draft will be available for inspection at PLANMalaysia Penang in Komtar, the Seberang Perai City Council, five District and Land Offices, and online through the e-Publicity 2.0 platform on PLANMalaysia Penang’s official website.
Alias said the RSN is an official legal document under the Town and Country Planning Act 1976 that will guide major policies and proposals involving land use, the economy and the environment once gazetted.
“We understand that development must take place. It must be sustainable, and we must blend and balance the needs of economic growth, environmental preservation, and social inclusivity,” he said.

Title: Ranau court fines duo RM3,500 each after Sabah police link their wrist marks to illegal militant Philippine group
Article:
RANAU, Aug 17 — Two men were each fined RM3,500 by the Ranau Magistrate’s Court for being members of a Philippine organisation deemed illegal under the Societies Act 1966 – the latest in such cases in the district.
Roy Martin, 35, a farmer, and Mohd Sharin Ibrahim, 40, a tyre mechanic, were charged under Section 43 of the Societies Act 1966 for being members of Kappa Rho Kappa (KRK), also referred to in the investigation as the Knights of the Right Keppers, a Philippines-based militant organisation.
The court imposed a fine of RM3,500 on each accused, with six months’ imprisonment in default of payment.
The cases stemmed from a police operation conducted on June 5, 2026, at about 10.50am at HH Rich, Kg Kinasaraban, Ranau, under Op Tik Tok (Gangsterism).
More than an on-ground activation, Hotlink Prepaid Pasti Mampu Belanja Makan celebrated the spirit of Sabah's Geng Bijak Berbajet, people who know that spending wisely doesn't mean settling for less, but finding smarter ways to enjoy more.
According to the case documents, a team from the D7 Criminal Investigation Department (JSJ) of the Sabah Police Contingent Headquarters, led by Insp Jesmera bin Bandong, conducted checks on the two men at the premises.
During the inspection, police reportedly discovered three cigarette-burn marks on the upper part of the men’s right wrists, which investigators suspected to be associated with KRK membership.
Police also seized two mobile phones – a blue Redmi belonging to one of the men and an orange Realme phone belonging to the other – which were found to contain videos allegedly displaying content associated with the group.
The investigation subsequently sought verification from a gang-related crime expert, who confirmed that one of the accused was believed to be a member of the group based on the identifying marks found on his wrist.
Further checks with the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (ROS) Sabah also established that Kappa Rho Kappa (KRK) was not legally registered with the department. — Daily Express

Title: No water for nearly two months, then a RM120,000 bill — Putatan  condo dwellers ask why pay for water Sabah water utility was already treating
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — Residents of Kingfisher Putatan Condominium (KFP) are refusing to pay the more than RM120,000 bill for water delivered by privately-operated tankers when they endured 55 days without supply between April and May.
Some said they had no choice but to purchase bottled water for drinking, washing, cooking, cleaning and other daily needs. They said the extra expenses should not have been necessary if the State Water Department (JANS) had fulfilled its responsibility.
Despite being located just south of Kota Kinabalu, Putatan has faced repeated water shortages since 2018. During the disruption, the condominium’s developer and management, Hap Seng Land Development and JCA Sdn Bhd, were compelled to procure water from private tankers.
However, residents later discovered that the water delivered was treated water originating from JANS itself; the same supply that had failed to reach them through the normal distribution network.
More than an on-ground activation, Hotlink Prepaid Pasti Mampu Belanja Makan celebrated the spirit of Sabah’s Geng Bijak Berbajet, people who know that spending wisely doesn’t mean settling for less, but finding smarter ways to enjoy more.
This emergency procurement drove costs up significantly, with residents charged RM7.50 per cubic metre after deducting the standard tariff of RM1.30 per cubic metre.
Many residents have refused to settle the outstanding bill, arguing they should not bear the financial burden of failures in the public water distribution system.
“The water we paid for was not from an alternative utility. It was JANS-treated water, only transported at higher logistical costs,” one resident said, questioning why consumers should be penalised for systemic shortcomings.
The crisis has left residents frustrated, with repeated interruptions continuing to affect sanitation, hygiene, cooking and daily living. The situation raised concerns that prolonged disruptions could escalate into a public health issue if not urgently addressed.
They are calling for accountability from the authorities, stressing that the government, as the primary duty-bearer, must ensure reliable access to clean water and sanitation.
After all, the government is legally and ethically responsible for ensuring clean water and sanitation infrastructure, although accountability is shared across multiple levels, including state agencies, utility operators, and regulatory bodies.
They are calling on the authorities to take concrete action to avoid legal intervention. Such a basic need and right for citizens, they argue, has been neglected. — Daily Express

Title: Century‑old Penang Hill railway gets track and roof repairs in scheduled January 2027 break
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — Penang Hill’s iconic funicular will take a short break from January 4 to 10, 2027 for its scheduled bi annual maintenance, Penang Hill Corporation (PHC) announced today. Service is set to resume on January 11.
Engineers from Swiss manufacturer Garaventa AG will oversee the works, which include repairs to the Lower Station track structure, as well as upgrades to the funicular’s air conditioning system and roof. PHC said the shutdown is part of routine safety checks designed to keep the hill’s century old railway running smoothly.
During the closure, visitors can use the jeep service operated by the Penang Hill Jeep Service Association near the Penang Botanic Gardens Department Office, or take existing hiking routes to the summit.

Title: Sarawak forest fire in Daro enters eighth day, 4ha still burning
Article:
DARO, Aug 17 — Firefighters are on their eighth day of working to extinguish a forest fire in Kampung Kut here, which has affected about 29ha of land.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said in a statement that firefighters are working to completely extinguish the remaining hotspots of the forest fire.
About 4ha of the affected area remained unextinguished as of Sunday.
Firefighters from the Daro fire station were deployed to three sectors during the operation.
“Sector one is located behind a petrol station, sector two along the main road, while sector three is near a telecommunications tower,” said Bomba.
Firefighting operations continued until 5pm, with two excavators deployed to create firebreaks to prevent the blaze from spreading further.
Firefighters also used water from nearby drains and a check dam to support suppression efforts.
A distress call on the fire was first received at around 1.40pm on Aug 10. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kuching man loses RM104,310 after falling for WhatsApp scam from friend’s hijacked account
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 17 — A 49-year-old man here lost RM104,310 to a phone scam last week.
Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the victim was contacted via WhatsApp from a friend’s number, but it turned out the account had been hacked and hijacked.
“Last Thursday when the victim was in his office, he received a message from the number that belonged to his friend seeking help to make payments for the purchase of an item.
“Having trusted the message, the victim then made four transfers to three different accounts from Aug 13 to Aug 15, amounting to a total sum of RM104,310.
“On Aug 15, he was informed by his friend that the WhatsApp account was believed to have been hacked, saying he did not request the victim to make such transfers,” Alexson said in a statement.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and dishonestly inducing the delivery of property.
The Section provides for imprisonment of up to 10 years, caning, and a fine upon conviction.
Alexson reminded the public to be vigilant against such scam tactics by ceasing any suspicious correspondences immediately, not providing any personal or banking information to unknown individuals, and to contact the nearest police station to conduct checks or lodge a report.
“Members of the public are advised to conduct prior checks before making payments to a third party and to check suspicious accounts and phone numbers via the Semak Mule PDRM link at https://semakmule.rmp.gov.my,” he added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Johor businessman’s body bound in net, dumped in river; four accused face murder charge
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Aug 17 — Four men were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here with murdering a businessman, whose body was bound and covered in a net before being found in a river earlier this month.
The accused — S. Yogesvaran, 40; Lim Yong Ming, 26; N. Achutan, 32; and How Han Wei, 33 — nodded to indicate they understood the charge after it was read before Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno in Bahasa Melayu.
However, no plea was recorded as cases under Section 302 of the Penal Code fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
According to the charge, the men were accused of murdering Low Kai Xian, 39, between 2.35pm on July 29 in front of the Sinhai Sdn Bhd restaurant in Jalan Emas Putih 2, Taman Sri Skudai, Johor Bahru, and 12.30pm on August 3 in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong here.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and, if the death penalty is not imposed, whipping of not less than 12 strokes upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim appeared for the prosecution, while Yogesvaran, Yong Ming and Han Wei were represented by counsel S.J. Sean Dudley. Achutan was represented by his counsel Datin Freda Sabapathy.
Present for a watching brief during the proceedings were lawyers, Chuan Shyie Chien and Kenji Soh Xin Da, who were representing the victim’s family.
The court set October 14 for mention and the submission of the autopsy and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) reports. This is in addition to submitting the closed-circuit television (CCTV) and mobile phone forensics.
Previously, it was reported that police arrested five suspects following the discovery of a 39-year-old businessman’s body floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, earlier this month.
The body, believed to be dumped in the river, was found bound and covered in a net, by the nearby residents.
Investigators also found five rocks placed with the victim’s body to weigh down the remains and prevent the body from surfacing.
The victim was later identified as a Johor Bahru-based businessman from Iskandar Puteri and had been reported missing since July 29.
He was identified by his next of kin based on his clothing and personal belongings.
Police said the motive for the murder may have been linked to debt.

Title: Pantai firefighters extinguish blaze on Jalan Kerinchi, BMW destroyed, Axia 30 per cent damaged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A BMW was destroyed and a Perodua Axia partially damaged after a blaze broke out at KL Gateway Mall, Jalan Kerinchi, last night.
The Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call via the NG999 line at 9.53pm before dispatching six firefighters from the Pantai station to the scene,
New Straits Times
reported.
Operations commander Mokhtar Ramli said firefighters found two vehicles at the scene — the BMW was completely gutted, while the Perodua Axia sustained about 30 per cent damage.
The fire was brought under control and extinguished. The cause is under investigation.

Title: Sarawak air quality improves as Serian and Samarahan drop from unhealthy to moderate
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 17 — Sarawak recorded moderate air quality at all monitoring stations except Bario, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading remained at good level as of 8am on Monday, according to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s Daily Haze Watch.
Air quality in Serian and Samarahan improved from unhealthy levels — with API readings of 157 and 151 respectively at 4pm on Sunday — to moderate levels of 98 and 92 by 8am.
Lundu and Tebedu also improved, dropping from unhealthy readings of 111 and 109 at 4pm on Sunday to 93 and 73 respectively by 8am.
However, three areas recorded slight increases in API readings. They were Sibu, rising from 66 at 4pm on Sunday to 70 by 8am; Kapit (from 52 to 54); and Lubok Antu (from 68 to 70).
Samalaju registered the biggest drop, from 79 at 4pm on Sunday to 62 by 8am, followed by Miri (from 79 to 65), Industrial Training Institute Miri (from 75 to 62), Limbang (from 68 to 52).
Kuching’s API reading also fell further to 87 by 8am, seven points lower than 4pm on Sunday.
Other locations with decreasing readings were Sri Aman, from 84 at 4pm on Sunday to 80 by 8am; Sarikei (from 76 to 75); Bintulu (from 70 to 67); Mukah (from 59 to 57).
Lawas remained unchanged at 67, while Bario’s recorded 50.
An API reading ranging from 51 to 100 is classified as moderate, while API readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as good. — The Borneo Post

Title: Man, 35, dies after motorcycle strikes lorry left without fuel on Tumpat flyover
Article:
TUMPAT, Aug 17 — A 35-year-old motorcyclist was killed when his Yamaha 135LC struck the rear of a parked lorry on the Wakaf Bharu flyover here yesterday evening.
The accident happened at about 5pm as the victim was riding from Kota Bharu towards Pengkalan Kubor,
Berita Harian
(BH) reported.
Tumpat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said the lorry had been left on the left shoulder of the flyover after running out of fuel. The victim was believed to have collided with its right rear section while negotiating a bend.
He told BH that the man suffered severe chest injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical assistant. The body was later sent to Tumpat Hospital for a post mortem, which confirmed the cause of death as multiple fatal injuries sustained in the crash.
Police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Members of the public with information are urged to contact the Tumpat district traffic investigation officer at 09 7257222 or visit the district traffic office.

Title: Religious leaders launch Tabung Haji RCI outreach, clarify misuse risks and safeguard 9.7 million depositors’ savings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Efforts to explain the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will be extended nationwide to help the public gain a comprehensive understanding of how the institution’s deposits were managed.
Former Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa said the initiative would see Islamic scholars and religious figures explaining the RCI TH findings through mosques, surau, schools, government departments, colleges, universities and community education platforms.
He said the initiative followed a special conference, Hifz al-Mal, which brought together more than 100 scholars and religious leaders from across the country yesterday to discuss the findings and the responsibility of safeguarding the savings of 9.7 million depositors.
“The objective is clear: the facts must be explained, the trust must be upheld, and the misuse of the people’s assets must not be allowed to happen again. Tabung Haji is a trust held on behalf of the Muslim community. Protecting it is our shared responsibility,” he said in a Facebook post.
Mujahid, who is also Amanah deputy president, said the Malaysian Ulama Secretariat organised the conference at De Palma Hotel in Ampang in collaboration with Malaysian Ulama Council Mursyid al-’Am (Spiritual Leader) Abdul Rahim Abdul Rahman.
“What makes the conference particularly significant is that it brought together religious figures alongside professionals and scholars from various fields, including chartered accountants, economic commentators, legal practitioners, religious educators and pondok scholars.
“This combination of expertise allows a more comprehensive discussion of the RCI findings on Tabung Haji, covering religious, financial, economic, accounting, legal and governance aspects, as well as the responsibility of safeguarding the community’s assets,” he said.
Among the main sessions was an examination of the RCI findings from a professional perspective, as well as the roles of religious figures and the community in understanding and safeguarding the trust placed in them.
Mujahid said the conference was founded on the principle of Hifz al-Mal, or the protection of wealth, particularly given TH’s role in managing the savings of millions of Muslims to fund their haj pilgrimage. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar moves to amend Tabung Haji Act, vows stronger governance to safeguard Muslim trust
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The government will amend the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) to ensure that the trust of Muslims continues to be safeguarded, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, also the Finance Minister, said the amendment was among the Madani Government’s measures to strengthen governance and ensure that every institutional weakness was addressed firmly.
“Governance must continue to be strengthened, institutions cleaned up and every weakness firmly addressed. The Tabung Haji Act will be amended to safeguard the trust of Muslims.
“… meanwhile AUKU (Universities and University Colleges Act) 1971 must be completely repealed without being replaced by a new law that continues to restrict students’ voices,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
In the same post, the Prime Minister said that the Madani Government under his leadership would continue to ensure that economic growth translated into a better quality of life for the people, regardless of their political or state background.
He said people in opposition-led states also deserved to be looked after, as the government’s responsibility was not only to its supporters or certain states, but to the entire people and the nation.
In conjunction with the 2026 Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) National Congress that concluded yesterday, Anwar, who is also the PKR president, said the party had chosen the path of principles, idealism and courage to do what was right, by not compromising principles or betraying the ideals of reform merely to defend power.
He stressed that PKR must remain a platform for the struggle for all Malaysians across race, religion and region, with the principle of justice demonstrated through policies and actions.
“Keadilan’s strength relies on a clean team, strong leadership and organised efforts. Strength is not a tool to enrich oneself, one’s family or cronies, but a trust to champion the people, uphold justice and elevate human dignity.
“Close ranks, streamline efforts and continue moving forward for the people and the nation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Explained: Can a person be charged in a Malaysian hospital instead of a courtroom?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Did you know that an accused person can be charged or face trial while hospitalised in Malaysia, instead of waiting for them to appear in court?
Here’s what criminal lawyers told Malay Mail about when and why this can happen:
1. Can an accused person be charged in a hospital ward?
Short answer: Yes.
Senior criminal lawyer Datuk N. Sivananthan confirmed this can be done.
“Yes, the ward can be declared as open court and the proceedings can take place as if one was in the actual court concerned,” he said.
Besides hospital wards, Sivananthan said a person could also be charged at other locations outside court.
“You can declare any place as an open court.”
He cited three legal provisions that enable this: Section 7 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC), and Sections 15 and 15A of the Courts of Judicature Act (CJA).
Sections 7 and 15 enable “the place” where any court is held for a criminal case to be treated as an “open and public court” where the public generally may have access, while Section 15A further enables court proceedings to be conducted online.
Based on Section 15, Sivananthan said it is possible for a court to decide to charge someone outside a courtroom while disallowing public access to the hospital ward by deciding that the matter is “in camera” or to be held privately.
Section 15 states that the court can decide to hear a case “in camera” for reasons such as the interests of justice, public safety, public security or propriety.
Former Malaysian Bar president Salim Bashir Bhaskaran said an accused would in “ordinary circumstances” be charged in a courtroom, but the Subordinate Courts Act gives magistrates and Sessions Court judges the power to declare “an open space or confined areas like hospitals, nursing homes” or police stations or prisons as a court.
Section 76(3) of the Subordinate Courts Act states that a Magistrates’ Court can be held at any other place if there is a need to do so, while Section 59(4) similarly says a Sessions Court can be held at any other place if the necessity arises.
Criminal lawyer Rajsurian Pillai said an accused person can be charged at a physical location other than the usual courtroom, including at a hospital.
“This has happened on previous occasions in Malaysia. Therefore, there is nothing inherently irregular about a hospital being the physical venue where a charging proceeding takes place,” he told Malay Mail, adding that court proceedings before judges would not be invalid just because they are held outside a courtroom.
He said this is consistent with Sections 173(a) and 178(1) of the CPC, which require an accused person to appear or be brought before a magistrate or High Court judge for the charge to be read and explained before a plea is recorded.
“Neither provision makes the physical courtroom itself the essential requirement.”
“Accordingly, where an accused is hospitalised or otherwise physically unable to attend the usual courtroom, the court may, where appropriate, conduct the relevant proceedings at another location, taking into account matters such as the accused’s medical condition, the urgency and circumstances of the case, and the interests of justice,” he said, noting that this would be determined on a case-by-case basis.
He stressed that the important point is that a High Court judge or judicial officer — a Sessions Court judge or magistrate — is conducting the proceedings, and that the usual procedural and legal safeguards for criminal cases are complied with during proceedings held outside the courtroom.
2. Prosecution has to apply to charge an accused in hospital
To have an accused person charged in a hospital ward, Sivananthan said the prosecution would have to apply to the judge where the charge is registered.
He noted that the accused person’s defence lawyers “cannot object unless the accused is not fit enough to understand the proceedings”.
He said police would check with doctors in advance on the accused person’s health condition before the judge decides whether to have the charges read out in the hospital ward.
If the court agrees to have the accused charged in the hospital ward, the relevant equipment to record the proceedings and personnel, including court police and court staff, would have to be present in the ward, he said.
3. What reasons might result in a person being charged in a hospital?
When asked what reasons the prosecution might use to apply for a person to be charged in a hospital, Sivananthan said:
“If a charge keeps getting delayed because the accused is constantly in hospital for one reason or the other.”
Salim said the prosecution would try to ask the court to consider charging an accused person in hospital when there is an “exceptional situation of need”, adding that this “is subjective and varies based on an urgency of a matter, and is to avoid unnecessary delays due to health conditions of the accused”.
Salim said the “judge or magistrate will assess the request from prosecution primarily based on the accused’s health conditions and advice from health officers”.
4. What happens when a person is charged in a hospital ward?
If carried out in a hospital, Salim said the procedure would be “the same” as an ordinary court process, where an interpreter would read out the charge to an accused person who is conscious, and the nature and consequences of pleading guilty or not guilty must be explained before the person’s plea is recorded.
Sivananthan said the judge has to be at the hospital ward, declare it an open court, and proceed to have the charge read out, the plea recorded and the bail amount set if bail is granted.
“The ward must allow for access by lawyers and the public which is a requirement of an open court.”
He said police would then have to be on standby to guard the accused until bail is paid, or ensure that the accused is taken into custody once discharged from hospital if no bail is given.
5. What about remand and trials? Can they happen in hospitals too?
Short answer: Yes.
Rajsurian said remand proceedings and trials can take place physically outside the conventional courtroom, noting that remand proceedings could, for example, take place in mobile courts.
Rajsurian said he had represented clients in remand proceedings before magistrates at police lock-ups, halls at district police headquarters and hospitals.
Salim said Section 117 of the CPC “allows remand proceedings to take place at any locations before a magistrate”, as Section 117 does not mention the word “court” and only requires the accused to be brought before magistrates.
Based on Sections 7, 15 and 15A, Sivananthan also said both remand proceedings and trials can take place outside court by having such places declared an open court.
But while saying trials can “in theory” take place in hospitals, Sivananthan said this is “unlikely as there would be an issue whether the accused person can understand what is going on depending on his health condition”.
“That would also apply to a person being charged. The accused must be able to understand the charge and to follow proceedings as the case may be,” he said.
6. Yes, it can be done, but usually as a last resort
Salim said “conducting trials in hospitals should be the last resort”, as declaring hospitals as courts and holding trials there may prevent the public from having access to the hospital’s facilities “due to constraint of space or security reasons”.
Sivananthan said charging an accused outside the courtroom “has to be resorted to as a last resort”, as it is difficult due to reasons such as convenience, staff movement, police assignments and security at any other location.
Compared to the past, when everything in court proceedings was written down by hand, Malaysia’s courts now use a digital recording and voice-to-text transcription system, meaning that conducting proceedings elsewhere would be difficult, he said.
Pointing out that hospitals do not have courtroom facilities such as video recorders and microphones, Rajsurian said court proceedings would only be held at hospitals for “very urgent” cases where there are no other options.
For example, an accused would have to be urgently charged at the hospital during the police’s investigation period if it involved a drug trafficking offence under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act, which can be punishable with death or whipping and life imprisonment, Rajsurian said.
No bail can be given for a Section 39B offence as it involves a possible death penalty, which means the accused cannot be released and would have to be detained while waiting for the trial to be completed.
On August 7, initial news reports indicated that former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob could be charged at the National Heart Institute (IJN), where he had been hospitalised since the day before.
The Sessions Court allowed his case to be postponed to August 27 after his lawyers requested the postponement due to his pacemaker surgery for abnormal heart rhythm that afternoon. The prosecution did not object due to humanitarian reasons.
Screenshot from Malaysian Judiciary's 2016 Yearbook.
Four in-real-life cases
Based on the Malaysian Judiciary’s 2016 Yearbook, Suadin @ Shuhaiddin Langkab was admitted to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, before a court hearing. However, the Court of Appeal on September 23, 2016 decided to proceed with hearing his appeal against his two corruption convictions as the case had been postponed too many times.
This was after the hospital’s medical officers confirmed that Suadin was fit to attend the court hearing, despite his illness. The appeal hearing was carried out under medical supervision after the Court of Appeal declared the hospital ward an open court under Section 7 of the CPC.
In another case, a corruption charge was read to senior immigration officer Zulkifly Abd Za’Par before a Sessions Court judge at a hospital in Shah Alam on December 22, 2020, following the prosecution’s request to charge him there while he was being treated for high blood pressure and heart disease.
He had previously been unable to attend an earlier court proceeding on December 11 as he was receiving medical treatment.
On January 11, 2021, Zulkifly was charged at a private hospital in Johor Bahru, where he was being treated for high blood pressure, with 21 counts of accepting RM56,500 in bribes read out to him before another Sessions Court judge.
On May 6, 2025, 28-year-old beggar Mohamad Fauzan Adib Abd Aziz was charged in a ward at Shah Alam Hospital, where he was receiving medical treatment for seizures. News reports stated that he nodded to indicate he understood the charge — of allegedly murdering a fellow beggar — read out to him before a magistrate in closed-door proceedings.
On January 9, 2026, Yeoh Hock Sun, 63, pleaded not guilty to five charges over an explosion involving an improvised explosive device (IED) in Nilai, with the charges read out to him before a Sessions Court judge in closed-door proceedings at Hospital Tuanku Jaafar in Seremban, where he was reportedly being treated for injuries from the explosion.
Yeoh’s February 12 case mention was postponed as he was in critical condition. He was pronounced dead on February 27 at Hospital Kuala Lumpur due to refractory shock.

Title: Haze returns: What Malaysians need to know as air quality deteriorates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Malaysians are once again experiencing the unwelcome return of a familiar foe — the haze.
Residents in several states, including Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Sarawak, are grappling with deteriorating air quality.
As of Thursday (Aug 13) morning, air quality in 11 areas across the country was at unhealthy levels, with Sarawak the worst-affected state.
According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System portal, Samarahan recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 183, followed by Serian (182), Kuching (176), Sarikei and Sri Aman (158), while Mukah and Sibu each recorded readings of 152.
In Peninsular Malaysia, four areas recorded unhealthy readings: Johan Setia (154) and Shah Alam (101) in Selangor, as well as Kuala Lumpur (131) and Putrajaya (104).
Reports indicate that the current haze is largely caused by forest and land fires, primarily in neighbouring Indonesia, where extensive land-clearing practices are common.
Meteorologists have warned that without significant rainfall, the haze may persist, affecting air quality and public health across Malaysia.
Malaysia is susceptible to haze due to its geographical location and tropical climate, which contributes to high humidity and temperature fluctuations. — Picture by K.E. Ooi
What causes the haze?
Haze is a form of air pollution characterised by fine particulate matter suspended in the atmosphere.
These particles comprise various pollutants, particularly smoke, dust and industrial emissions, which combine with water vapour.
Malaysia is susceptible to haze due to its geographical location and tropical climate, which contributes to high humidity and temperature fluctuations.
Land-clearing practices, particularly for palm oil plantations and agricultural purposes, can also result in significant emissions when fires occur.
Smoke generated by these fires can drift across borders, severely affecting air quality in Malaysia, particularly in states closer to the source of the fires.
Haze has been a recurring environmental issue in Malaysia since the late 1990s, often linked to land-clearing methods and changing weather patterns, particularly during El Niño years.
Significant haze events were recorded in October 1997, lasting for several months and triggering international outcry and the mobilisation of resources to address the crisis.
In 2005 and 2015, severe transboundary haze from Indonesian agricultural fires forced widespread school closures across Malaysia.
In August 2005, a state of emergency was declared in Kuala Selangor and Port Klang after API readings exceeded 500, resulting in the closure of schools in the affected areas.
In October 2015, nearly 7,000 schools were closed nationwide as API readings reached hazardous levels.
How is haze measured?
In Malaysia, air quality is assessed using the API, which measures the concentration of various pollutants, including particulate matter.
The API is divided into several categories indicating the level of air quality:
Good (0-50): Air quality is satisfactory, posing little or no risk.
Moderate (51-100): Air quality is acceptable, although some people, particularly those unusually sensitive to air pollution, may be affected.
Unhealthy (101-200): Everyone may begin to experience health effects, while members of sensitive groups may experience more serious effects.
Very unhealthy (201-300): A health alert level at which everyone may experience more serious health effects.
Hazardous (301 and above): Health warnings of emergency conditions, with the entire population more likely to be affected.
As API levels rise, authorities typically issue health advisories and take measures such as closing schools or limiting outdoor activities.
At-risk groups and protective measures
Certain groups are particularly vulnerable during haze episodes, including children, the elderly, people with pre-existing respiratory or cardiovascular conditions, and pregnant women.
To reduce the risks associated with haze, those in at-risk groups should stay indoors as much as possible, use air purifiers, stay hydrated and limit strenuous outdoor activities.
Health authorities often recommend face masks, particularly N95 respirators, which can effectively filter fine particulate matter.
N95 masks are designed to filter out at least 95 per cent of airborne particles. — Bernama pic
How effective are masks?
Masks can help reduce exposure to haze, but not all masks provide the same level of protection.
N95 masks are designed to filter out at least 95 per cent of airborne particles.
However, during extremely high levels of pollution, even these masks may not provide complete protection against all harmful particles.
Haze can also infiltrate homes, further affecting indoor air quality. It is therefore important to monitor air quality levels and take additional measures where necessary.
Impact of El Niño on haze conditions
The El Niño phenomenon can significantly alter weather patterns, often resulting in prolonged dry spells that increase the likelihood of forest and land fires.
During El Niño years, higher temperatures and reduced rainfall can make it easier for fires to start and spread.
In Malaysia, stagnant air caused by limited wind movement can exacerbate haze, allowing it to linger for longer and creating a hazardous environment for residents.
The combination of adverse weather conditions and reduced air circulation can result in an extended period of poor air quality if the dry season persists.

Title: Farmer’s coconut dehusking invention gets a shot at cracking the durian market
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 17 — An innovative coconut dehusking device developed by plantation entrepreneur Che Adnan Che Kadir, 56, which received a four-star rating, could now be adapted for durians and commercialised to meet the needs of the agricultural industry.
Che Adnan said the judging panel at the Kelantan Department of Agriculture’s 2026 Agricultural Technology Innovation Competition proposed the idea after seeing the device’s potential for adaptation to other fruits.
“Durians and areca nuts were among the fruits suggested, with durians identified as the main target for further development because opening or cutting them open requires skill and careful handling.
“I feel even more motivated, and I never expected that something I designed for my own farm would now be considered for a wider market,” he told
Bernama
recently.
He said he received the farmer category award two days ago, which could see him selected to represent Kelantan at the national level during National Innovation Week in Putrajaya at the end of September.
Che Adnan said support from the Department of Agriculture allowed him to compete at the state level, where the invention was assessed by judges from the department, the Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi) and polytechnics.
“To compete at the national level, we need to make several improvements based on the judges’ recommendations…we hope to secure an innovation grant to refine the design and develop the product according to production capacity and industry needs,” he said.
He said the device was initially developed in 2024 to overcome the challenges of dehusking coconuts with traditional methods on his six-hectare farm in Kampung Chetok, Pasir Mas, while reducing the risk of injury and speeding up the process.
According to him, the 3.5kg device is portable and can cut the time needed to remove a coconut husk from 2 to 3 minutes by hand to about 1 minute, while skilled workers can do it in 40 to 45 seconds.
Che Adnan said he hoped that, once adapted for durians, the device could become a practical and safe home-grown innovation, while helping farmers and potentially reaching wider markets.
He said the national innovation grant, which comes with a RM10,000 prize, could help fine-tune the design and bring the innovation to market. — Bernama

Title: Mat Sabu launches book, warns Malaysians against propaganda, urges facts over allegations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Accepting allegations without proper scrutiny could fuel ‘asabiyyah’, a tendency to defend one’s own group even when it is at fault while viewing the good deeds of others negatively, said Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said the public should not accept information blindly, but instead verify the facts and gain a clearer understanding before taking a stand.
The Agriculture and Food Security Minister said the same approach should be adopted when assessing current political issues in the country.
"Claims have surfaced again that DAP is a communist party and that anyone who cooperates with it is therefore supporting communism. But is DAP really communist,” he told reporters after the launch of his book, Mustadhafin vs Mustakbirin, co-authored with Ennie Zuhasniza Jamaludin, here today.
The book was launched by National Journalism Laureate Tan Sri Johan Jaaffar, who is also a director of Star Media Group Berhad.
Mohamad said facts and knowledge were often harder to accept and took longer to digest, unlike accusations and suspicions that could spread easily, especially through social media.
Commenting on the book, he said it documents his experiences and meetings with various parties as he sought to understand issues based on the actual situation, rather than relying solely on information being circulated.
"From a young age, I would not immediately accept information I received. I preferred to find out for myself what was happening rather than simply listening to propaganda being circulated,” he said.
Mohamad said the book also offers his perspective on global geopolitical dynamics, drawing on his experiences, observations and thoughts, while touching on colonialism, the Islamic movement, the Palestinian conflict and shifts in global power. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian pilot detained in Jakarta, accused of smuggling RM45m drugs abroad since 2024
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — A local airline pilot, who was arrested in Indonesia last month in connection with the discovery of drugs worth RM45 million, is believed to have smuggled the illegal substances out of the country several times since 2024.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations found that the 39-year-old man is believed to have used his flight schedule to transport drugs to several destinations.
“This was not the first time, because he had transported drugs to several countries on several occasions,” he said when contacted.
He said the man’s activities were uncovered during interrogation by a team of NCID officers in Jakarta recently.
Hussein said the interrogation also led to the discovery of the existence of several drug trafficking syndicate networks operating in Malaysia and abroad, including Indonesia.
Following this, he said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is tracking down the remaining members of the syndicate involved and tracing the flow of proceeds from the drug trafficking activities, in addition to sharing the information with relevant international drug enforcement agencies.
Commenting on the suspect’s tactics in getting past stringent checks at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Hussein said investigations found that the man acted alone without the assistance of any “insider”.
“We are satisfied that there was no involvement of an insider in the process of the suspect passing through security checks at KLIA. However, the modus operandi used cannot be disclosed to avoid compromising the ongoing investigation,” he said.
He also expressed his appreciation to the Indonesian National Police (POLRI) for their close cooperation in assisting the investigation, especially during the interrogation of the suspect, which concluded on Friday (Aug 14).
Hussein had previously said that no extradition request would be made for the pilot, and that the suspect would have to undergo the legal process in Indonesia.
On July 29, the media reported that a 39-year-old pilot had been arrested by Indonesian authorities at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 25 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs.
According to POLRI, an inspection uncovered 15 packages containing 70,114 ecstasy and methamphetamine capsules, worth an estimated RM45 million based on Indonesian market prices. — Bernama

Title: Minister calls nine‑year abandoned Tambunan Hospital project ‘sick’, pledges RM988,000 for urgent upgrades
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 16 — The new Outpatient Department (OPD) building project at Tambunan Hospital, which has been abandoned for nine years, will be resumed to improve the comfort of patients and staff.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the situation at the hospital was among the most disheartening things he witnessed during his working visit there today, with patients and staff having to cope with limited space.
“InsyaAllah, we will revive this ‘sick’ project and ensure it is completed for the comfort and rights of the people of Tambunan,” he said in a Facebook post.
Dzulkefly also announced an immediate allocation of RM988,000 to address urgent needs at the hospital, with a large portion channelled towards upgrading the Emergency Department.
He said RM185,000 of the allocation would be used to repair the severely damaged canteen building to provide suitable dining facilities, while the remaining funds would go towards purchasing medical equipment and other necessary amenities.
He also thanked Keningau Member of Parliament and Tambunan state assemblyman Datuk Seri Dr Jeffrey Kitingan for contributing a hydraulic bed and an ultrasound machine to the hospital.
“This is in addition to the six hydraulic beds and one ultrasound machine that were also approved for Tambunan Hospital today. The responsibility of safeguarding the people’s health is made easier when all parties work together,” he said.
Regarding complaints about space at the Tambunan Dental Clinic, Dzulkefly said he had directed that the funding application to address the issue be expedited under the development budget planning for the 13th Malaysia Plan.
Operating since September 16, 1977, Tambunan Hospital is a non-specialist hospital under the Keningau Cluster with a capacity of 49 beds, serving about 43,400 residents across seven sub-districts and 88 villages.
The hospital provides 24-hour emergency and trauma care, as well as outpatient and inpatient services.
During the visit, Dzulkefly was also briefed on the hospital’s staffing situation, operational challenges and the distribution of supporting health facilities in Tambunan, which covers seven sub-districts and 88 villages. — Bernama

Title: USM climbs 149 places in Academic Ranking of World Universities, now Malaysia’s top university
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 16 — Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) has risen to become Malaysia’s top-ranked university in the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) 2026, climbing 149 places to rank 581st globally.
In a statement today, USM said the achievement marked an improvement from its 730th position last year and saw it move from third place nationally in 2025 to first place this year.
USM said the achievement was significant as ARWU, also known as ShanghaiRanking, evaluates universities based on academic and research performance rather than reputation or perception alone.
The ranking assesses factors including Nobel Prize and Fields Medal winners among alumni and staff, highly cited researchers (HiCi) recognised by Clarivate, publications in Nature and Science journals, publications indexed in the Science Citation Index-Expanded (SCIE) and Social Sciences Citation Index (SSCI), as well as academic performance per capita.
“Thirty per cent of the overall ARWU assessment is related to Nobel Prize and Fields Medal winners, while another 20 per cent is allocated to HiCi, meaning half of the evaluation is directly linked to world-class academic achievements and researchers with highly influential citations,” it said.
USM said more than 2,500 universities worldwide are assessed by ARWU annually, with only the top 1,000 included in the ranking, making its 149-place rise within a year a significant achievement.
In ARWU 2026, USM recorded strong performance in the Publication (PUB) indicator, ranking 424th globally, while its HiCi indicator improved to 503rd worldwide.
USM said the improvement in HiCi reflected that research produced by its academics was increasingly being cited, utilised and contributing to global knowledge development.
It said ARWU differs from rankings that focus solely on the number of publications as it also evaluates the influence of researchers and research outputs at the international level.
USM, an APEX university, said the rise from 730th to 581st globally and from third to first place in Malaysia reflected the strengthening of its overall research ecosystem. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan Health Department to monitor baby girl’s growth after testing positive for drugs
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 16 — The Kelantan Health Department (JKNK) will continue to monitor the development of a baby girl who tested positive for drugs after birth to identify effects on her mental development, growth and physical development.
JKNK deputy health director (Medical) Dr Rohana Daud said continuous monitoring is important to ensure any effects on the baby can be identified, and appropriate action can be taken at an early stage.
“An examination using the Finnegan Score showed that the baby’s score is now zero after receiving treatment.
“Based on the information obtained, the baby’s mother had taken tranquilisers, and its effects on the baby are unlikely to be prolonged. Instead, the baby only experienced withdrawal symptoms,” she told reporters after officiating Universiti Sains Malaysia’s (USM) House Officer Preparatory Course 2026 at USM Hospital, Kubang Kerian, here today.
On August 12, a baby girl tested positive for amphetamine and benzodiazepines after undergoing a urine screening at the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II here.
Following the screening, police detained the baby’s 30-year-old mother to assist investigations under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. — Bernama

Title: Minister warns against immoral behaviour, stresses mosques and surau must remain sacred spaces
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Aug 16 — Muslims have been urged to observe proper conduct and good morals and refrain from immoral behaviour, especially in places of worship such as mosques and surau.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs), Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, said mosques and surau are sacred places that must be respected and whose sanctity must be preserved.
“Remember, whatever we do is seen by Allah SWT. We cannot escape accountability, and Allah SWT will judge all our actions and wrongdoings.
“I urge everyone to observe proper conduct, uphold good morals and comply with the law,” he told reporters after officiating at the closing ceremony of the Syariah Lawyers’ Sports Programme (SUKPES) at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) here today.
He was speaking in response to questions about a case involving a former mosque caretaker and a married woman who were accused of attempting to engage in illicit sexual relations in a mosque mortuary in Melaka.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli said continuous efforts were being made to educate and guide people of all ages, from young people to senior citizens, on compliance with Islamic law and the importance of good character through a range of programmes at mosques and surau, as well as social media campaigns, including those aimed at strengthening families. — Bernama

Title: Widow of corporal electrocuted in Sabah to receive Sarawak rental aid, housing support
Article:
SIBU, Aug 16 — The widow of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, who died in an electric shock incident in Sabah on August 6, will receive aid under the Sarawak Rental Assistance Scheme (SRAS), said Sarawak Deputy Minister for Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang Ming Tee.
The Pelawan assemblyman said he would assist Tang Wei Wei, 39, in securing an affordable home, in addition to providing rental assistance under the scheme.
“We will find a suitable and affordable house for Tang and her children,” he said when met by reporters after visiting the family in Ulu Sungai Merah here today.
Tiang said the Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan (C) Tiong Hin Management Board had agreed to cover Tang’s children’s education expenses, including tuition fees, until they complete primary school.
Meanwhile, he said the government would bear the pre-school education expenses, including textbooks, for Tang’s youngest child, who is four years old.
Tiang said he would continue to assist the family, particularly with several legal matters that remain unresolved.
Chiu, 40, was among three policemen believed to have been electrocuted while moving a metal pole used to harvest coconuts outside the Weston Police Station in Beaufort.
He is survived by his widow and five daughters, aged between four and 11. — Bernama

Title: MACC arrests two policemen over RM14,000 traffic offence bribes on East Coast Expressway
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 16 — A police constable and a patrol officer have been detained on suspicion of soliciting and accepting bribes amounting to approximately RM14,000 in exchange for not taking action against several motorists who committed traffic offences on the East Coast Expressway (LPT) 2.
According to a source, the male personnel, in his 30s, was arrested at around 5.30pm yesterday when he appeared to give his statement at the Pahang Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office.
“Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect is believed to have conspired to commit the act with another patrol police officer between January and July 2026.
“The suspect is believed to have received the bribe money via fund transfer transactions into a third-party bank account believed to be used by the suspect,” said the source.
The man has now been remanded for five days until August 20 after Magistrate Ellyna Othman allowed MACC’s application at the Kuantan Magistrate’s Court this morning.
Meanwhile, the male patrol police officer in his 30s who was previously arrested on August 11 has had his remand extended by four days until August 19.
The remand extension order was issued by the same Magistrate today after the first remand application for the police officer expired today.
Meanwhile, Pahang MACC Director Mohamad Shukor Mahmud, when contacted, confirmed the arrest of both suspects and informed that the case is being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution warns poverty and drugs, not racial fears, are Malays’ real enemies
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — The position of Malays in the country is not threatened by the existence of other races, but by poverty and social problems such as drug addiction, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The Home Minister said the real threat to the Malays is when they continue to be plagued by poverty and serious drug addiction.
“I want to state that Malays and Muslims are not under threat because of other races in this country. Malays are not under threat because there are Chinese in this country. Malays are not under threat because there are Indians in this country.
“Malays are threatened if they are poor. Malays are under threat if they are the ones most involved in drug-related problems... that is the threat to the Malays,” said Saifuddin Nasution, who is currently performing the duties of PKR’s deputy president.
He said this in his winding-up speech at the PKR National Congress 2026 at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.
Citing data from the Ministry of Health and National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK), Saifuddin Nasution said that, on average, about 560 out of every 100,000 people are involved in drug addiction.
However, he pointed out that the figures showed a worrying trend in several Malay-majority states, which recorded rates exceeding 1,000 per 100,000 people.
“When I cite figures from Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu, in these states more than 1,000 per 100,000 people (are involved in drug addiction).
“This means that the biggest threat to the Malays is because Malay youths become involved in drugs. Whether by chance or not, the highest number is in the Malay (majority) states,” he said.
He said those aged between 15 and 39 recorded the highest involvement in the unhealthy activity, especially among those with an education level of up to the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM).
“When we do not focus on developing the states, you only bring up DAP, DAP, DAP, (but) you do not take care of the states, job opportunities do not exist, (and) young people are involved in drugs.
“If you ask me how Malays are threatened, Malays becoming involved in drugs is a threat to the Malay community,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Three towns choke on unhealthy API, Serian tops list as haze blankets Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Three areas, including two in Sarawak, recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the Serian district police headquarters recorded the highest API reading at 157, followed by Samarahan at 151.
In Selangor, Johan Setia also recorded an unhealthy API reading of 124.
Meanwhile, 65 other locations recorded moderate air quality levels.
The API scale is as follows: 0-50 (Good), 51-100 (Moderate), 101-200 (Unhealthy), 201-300 (Very Unhealthy) and above 300 (Hazardous).
API readings are released hourly, based on data from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak Education Department says Serian schools reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 16 — All primary and secondary schools under the Serian District Education Office (PPD) will operate as usual from tomorrow, the Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today.
It said any changes or latest updates would be announced from time to time, while schools have been reminded to prioritise the health and safety of students, teachers and school personnel.
“JPNS will continue to emphasise the welfare, health and safety of students, especially when facing hot weather or any unexpected weather conditions.
“Schools are reminded to follow the stipulated standard operating procedures and refer to the Ministry of Education Malaysia (MOE) Circular Letter No. 1 of 2019; Measures by the MOE to Ensure the Health and Safety of Students in Schools Located in Areas with Critical Haze Conditions dated Jan 15, 2019,” the statement said.
JPNS said all educational institutions under its supervision should also follow the guidelines contained in the MOE Circular Letter No. 3 of 2023; Guidelines for the Implementation of Outdoor Activities at Educational Institutions under the MOE During Hot Weather dated June 6, 2023.
It added that schools should stay updated by referring to the Department of Environment’s official portal and the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) to monitor air quality levels in their respective areas, while adhering to advice from the Ministry of Health to safeguard the well-being of students and education personnel. — Bernama

Title: Defend Malaysia’s ports, but identify firms abusing transshipment, says maritime expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Malaysia should firmly defend its reputation as a trusted trading and shipping hub while conducting thorough checks to identify companies that may be abusing its ports to circumvent United States tariffs, said maritime industry observer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy.
He said Malaysia should neither dismiss the concerns raised by the US nor allow broad allegations to cast doubt on the country’s entire maritime and logistics sector, stressing that authorities should demand evidence and investigate specific companies and cargoes.
“We should not become defensive about the US report. Ask for the evidence. Investigate it properly. Identify the companies and cargo involved. Then take action based on facts and the law,” he said in a statement today.
Jeyenderan said Malaysia had worked hard to establish itself as a trusted regional shipping and trading hub, adding that any doubts over the credibility of Malaysian certificates of origin or cargo controls could have serious consequences for legitimate businesses.
“Once international partners start questioning our certificates of origin or our cargo controls, every genuine Malaysian company will suffer. Transshipment is not illegal.
“Malaysia is a major trading nation and cargo must be allowed to move through our ports. But legitimate transshipment must be clearly separated from any attempt to conceal the true origin of goods,” he said.
He said authorities should focus on discrepancies between bills of lading, customs declarations, certificates of origin, commercial invoices and the actual movement or handling of cargo.
He added that particular attention should be given to shipments where Chinese-origin goods are allegedly repacked, relabelled or subjected to minimal processing in Malaysia before being exported and declared as Malaysian-origin products.
“Changing a label or packaging does not automatically change the origin of a product. Authorities must establish whether genuine manufacturing or substantial transformation took place in Malaysia,” he said.
Jeyenderan said investigations should go beyond the physical container and identify the companies and intermediaries behind suspicious shipments, including importers, exporters, manufacturers, freight forwarders, customs agents, warehouse operators and commodity traders.
“If a company is deliberately using Malaysia to hide the true origin of goods, identify that company. We should not allow the entire Malaysian port industry to be blamed for the actions of a few companies,” he said.
Jeyenderan called for the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to strengthen risk-based screening by examining companies’ compliance histories, shipment volumes, declared values, countries of origin, consignee changes and unusual routing patterns.
Rather than physically inspecting every container, he said Customs could use data analytics to identify high-risk companies and shipments for targeted documentary and physical checks.
He also called for stronger information-sharing between Customs, port operators, shipping lines, enforcement agencies and relevant ministries to establish a digital audit trail covering high-risk cargo from its original port to its final destination.
“The authorities should be able to establish where the goods originated, who owned them, who handled them in Malaysia, whether substantial processing took place and where they were eventually exported,” he said.
He said post-clearance audits should also be strengthened because scrutiny should not end once a container leaves the port, particularly where goods are subsequently exported to markets with significantly different tariff treatment.
At the same time, Jeyenderan cautioned against excessive enforcement that could burden legitimate Malaysian manufacturers, exporters and logistics companies whose supply chains involve China or the US.
“Malaysia must be defensive of its reputation, not defensive against investigation. We should have nothing to fear from proper scrutiny if our systems are working,” he said.
“If companies are abusing our ports or free zones, identify them and take action. If the trade is legitimate, Malaysia should have the confidence to defend it,” he said.
Jeyenderan said the strongest response to the US concerns was therefore greater transparency, company-level accountability and evidence-based enforcement.
“Defend Malaysia’s ports. Protect legitimate businesses. But expose those who misuse the system. That is how we protect Malaysia’s reputation as a trusted trading nation,” he said.

Title: Saifuddin: End identity politics, focus on performance and economic recovery
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — PKR has called for an end to identity and racial politics, instead urging a greater focus on performance-based politics and economic recovery for the well-being of the people.
PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, who is discharging the duties of the deputy president, said identity politics was merely a “zero-sum game” that would bring no benefit to the country’s future.
“Do not fight in the arena of identity or racial politics because there are no winners there. We urge the people to evaluate us based on performance-based politics, namely economic performance and their well-being.
“Our politics is about making the ‘pie of prosperity’ bigger. We do not need to take away anyone’s rights to ensure that our children are well fed,” he said when delivering his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Saifuddin Nasution, who is also Home Minister, stressed that Malaysia’s racial diversity is a reality that must be accepted and should not be used as an instrument to sow fear among the people.
“Malay identity, Islamic identity, Chinese identity, Indian identity, Sabah identity and Sarawak identity are all part of the reality of Malaysia. There is nothing wrong with identity. The problem arises when identity is used to create fear,” he said.
In this regard, he outlined three key approaches that the Madani Government and party leadership should focus on, namely driving economic growth (“grow the pie”) through the concept of “making the pie of prosperity bigger” so that its benefits can be enjoyed by all segments of society.
The second approach is to channel assistance based on the people’s actual needs regardless of skin colour (need-based), while the third priority is to continue the good governance agenda and combat corruption that causes losses to the nation’s coffers.
He also stressed that the real threat to any community is not the presence of other races, but poverty and social problems such as drug abuse that damage the younger generation.
He said all party members must step up efforts to spread the success stories of the Madani Government and give particular focus to young voters ahead of the next election. — Bernama

Title: Status quo for now, DAP delegates vote to stay in govt
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP delegates today overwhelmingly voted for the party to remain in the federal government until the end of the current parliamentary term.
Congress speaker Cha Kee Chin announced that 1,857 delegates voted to stay, while 242 voted to leave the government.
Of the 2,106 delegates who voted, seven ballots were spoiled.
In a press conference after the results were announced, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the outcome gave the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) and its leaders in government a mandate to continue serving and pursuing reforms.
“So, this is a mandate to the CEC and to the party leaders representing the party in the government to continue serving, to continue our work, to continue the reform agenda, and to focus on implementing the changes and promises that we have made in the Pakatan Harapan manifesto.
“This is a responsibility and mandate that has been given by the delegates to us at the leadership level,” he said.
Loke also defended the turnout, saying attendance of more than half of eligible delegates was considered high for a DAP national congress, particularly as delegates were drawn from party branches across the country.
He said many delegates were small business owners, hawkers and traders who had to return to their businesses rather than attend the congress.
“Not everyone can attend. Even when there is a party election, usually only about 70 per cent attend. In fact, having more than half of the delegates attending is considered very high for a DAP national congress,” he said.
Loke said DAP would respect the 12 per cent of delegates who voted to leave the government, but the party must follow the decision of the 88 per cent majority.
“I respect the 12 per cent who made that decision. That is their opinion. They believe in it. They are not influenced. They are free to vote.
“But as a party, we also need to follow the opinion of the majority. The majority has made their decision with the confidence of the majority, the 88 per cent,” he said.
Loke said the decision was also intended to prevent political instability, stressing that delegates understood the need for DAP to work with Umno as part of the unity government.
“We do not want to create instability in the government.
“As I said, the delegates have decided that we should remain in the government. This is their expectation, knowing that we need to work with Umno. This is a political reality that all the delegates understand,” he said.
He said the decision was brought to the national congress precisely because the party wanted to respect the democratic process.
“That is why we brought this to the National Congress. We need to respect the democratic process. That is why I brought this to the National Congress and they made the decision,” he said.
Loke also rejected suggestions that DAP had used the congress vote to pressure Anwar into adopting its own political agenda, saying the reforms advocated by the party were jointly agreed upon by Pakatan Harapan and the unity government.
“We know our political opponents say that we want to use this convention or congress to pressure the Prime Minister with the DAP agenda.
“The DAP agenda is an agenda that has been jointly agreed upon within Pakatan Harapan and jointly agreed upon within the unity government,” he said.
He pointed to the proposed separation of the roles of Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, a two-term limit for the prime minister and efforts to combat corruption as examples of reforms that were not solely DAP initiatives.
“There are several reforms that have already been implemented immediately. For example, the separation of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor roles. That is an agenda that has been jointly agreed upon.
“The agenda to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure to two terms, that is a joint agenda.
“The agenda to fight corruption, that is a joint agenda. It is not solely a DAP agenda,” he said.
Loke also cited the implementation of e-invoicing as an example of a reform that had support within the unity government, noting that the initiative had also been brought to Cabinet by Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said DAP had been advocating the measure for a long time.
The vote took place after DAP’s national congress today debated whether the party should remain in the federal government or withdraw while continuing to support the administration from outside.
The debate followed DAP’s electoral setbacks in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with several delegates calling for the party to remain in government but push harder for reforms and better delivery.
